verses.20: οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ γένηται ἔτι ἐκεῖ ἄωρος καὶ πρεσβύτης, ὃς οὐκ ἐμπλήσει τὸν χρόνον αὐτοῦ· ἔσται γὰρ ὁ νέος ἐκατὸν ἐτῶν, ὁ δὲ ἀποθνήσκων ἁμαρτωλὸς ἑκατὸν ἐτῶν, καὶ ἐπικατάρατος ἔσται.
verses.21: Καὶ οἰκοδομήσουσιν οἰκίας, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνοικήσουσι· καὶ καταφυτεύσουσιν ἀμπελῶνας, καὶ αὐτοὶ φάγονται τὰ γεννήματα αὐτῶν.
verses.22: Οὐ μὴ οἰκοδομήσουσι, καὶ ἄλλοι ἐνοικήσουσι, καὶ οὐ μὴ φυτεύσουσι, καὶ ἄλλοι φάγονται· κατὰ γὰρ τὰς ἡμέρας τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς ἔσονται αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ λαοῦ μου· τὰ γὰρ ἔργα τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν παλαιώσουσιν.
verses.23: Οἱ ἐκλεκτοί μου οὐ κοπιάσουσιν εἰς κενὸν, οὐδὲ τεκνοποιήσουσιν εἰς κατάραν, ὅτι σπέρμα εὐλογημένον ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ἐστι, καὶ τὰ ἔκγονα αὐτῶν μετʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.24: Καὶ ἔσται πρὶν ἢ κεκράξαι αὐτοὺς, ἐγὼ ὑπακούσομαι αὐτῶν· ἔτι λαλούντων αὐτῶν, ἐρῶ, τί ἐστι;
verses.25: Τότε λύκοι καὶ ἄρνες βοσκηθήσονται ἅμα, καὶ λέων ὡς βοῦς φάγεται ἄχυρα, ὄφις δὲ γῆν ὡς ἄρτον· οὐκ ἀδικήσουσιν, οὐδὲ λυμανοῦνται ἐπὶ τῷ ὄρει τῷ ἁγίῳ μου, λέγει Κύριος.

verses.1: Υἱέ, μὴ ζηλώσῃς κακοὺς ἄνδρας, μηδὲ ἐπιθυμήσῃς εἶναι μετʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.2: Ψευδῆ γὰρ μελετᾷ ἡ καρδία αὐτῶν, καὶ πόνους τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν λαλεῖ.
verses.3: Μετὰ σοφίας οἰκοδομεῖται οἶκος, καὶ μετὰ συνέσεως ἀνορθοῦται.
verses.4: Μετὰ αἰσθήσεως ἐμπίμπλανται ταμιεῖα ἐκ παντὸς πλούτου τιμίου καὶ καλοῦ.
verses.5: Κρείσσων σοφὸς ἰσχυροῦ, καὶ ἀνὴρ φρόνησιν ἔχων γεωργίου μεγάλου.
verses.6: Μετὰ κυβερνήσεως γίνεται πόλεμος, βοήθεια δὲ μετὰ καρδίας βουλευτικῆς.
verses.7: Σοφία καὶ ἔννοια ἀγαθὴ ἐν πύλαις σοφῶν· σοφοὶ οὐκ ἐκκλίνουσιν ἐκ στόματος Κυρίου,
verses.8: ἀλλὰ λογίζονται ἐν συνεδρίοις· ἀπαιδεύτοις συναντᾷ θάνατος,
verses.9: ἀποθνήσκει δὲ ἄφρων ἐν ἁμαρτίαις· ἀκαθαρσία δὲ ἀνδρὶ λοιμῷ,
verses.10: ἐμμολυνθήσεται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῇ, καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως ἕως ἂν ἐκλίπῃ.
verses.11: Ῥῦσαι ἀγομένους εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἐκπρίου κτεινομένους, μὴ φείσῃ.
verses.12: Ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃς, οὐκ οἶδα τοῦτον, γίνωσκε, ὅτι Κύριος καρδίας πάντων γινώσκει· καὶ ὁ πλάσας πνοὴν πᾶσιν, αὐτὸς οἶδε πάντα, ὃς ἀποδίδωσιν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
verses.13: Φάγε μέλι υἱὲ, ἀγαθὸν γὰρ κηρίον, ἵνα γλυκανθῇ σου ὁ φάρυγξ.
verses.14: Οὕτως αἰσθητήσῃ σοφίαν τῇ σῇ ψυχῇ· ἐὰν γὰρ εὕρῃς, ἔσται καλὴ ἡ τελευτή σου, καὶ ἐλπίς σε οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψει.
verses.15: Μὴ προσαγάγῃς ἀσεβῆ νομῇ δικαίων, μηδὲ ἀπατηθῇς χορτασίᾳ κοιλίας.
verses.16: Ἑπτάκις γὰρ πεσεῖται δίκαιος καὶ ἀναστήσεται, οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς ἀσθενήσουσιν ἐν κακοῖς.
verses.17: Ἐὰν πέσῃ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, μὴ ἐπιχαρῇς αὐτῷ, ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποσκελίσματι αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπαίρου.
verses.18: Ὅτι ὄψεται Κύριος καὶ οὐκ ἀρέσει αὐτῷ, καὶ ἀποστρέψει τὸν θυμὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.19: Μὴ χαῖρε ἐπὶ κακοποιοῖς, μηδὲ ζήλου ἁμαρτωλούς.
verses.20: Οὐ γὰρ μὴ γένηται ἔκγονα πονηρῷ, λαμπτὴρ δὲ ἀσεβῶν σβεσθήσεται.
verses.21: Φοβοῦ τὸν Θεὸν υἱὲ, καὶ βασιλέα, καὶ μηθʼ ἑτέρῳ αὐτῶν ἀπειθήσῃς.
verses.22: Ἐξαίφνης γὰρ τίσονται τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς, τὰς δὲ τιμωρίας ἀμφοτέρων τίς γνώσεται;
verses.22a: Λόγον φυλασσόμενος υἱὸς ἀπωλείας ἐκτὸς ἔσται, [δεχόμενος δὲ ἐδέξατο αὐτόν·
verses.22b: μηδὲν ψεῦδος ἀπὸ γλώσσης βασιλεῖ λεγέσθω, καὶ οὐδὲν ψεῦδος ἀπὸ γλώσσης αὐτοῦ οὐ μή ἐξέλθῃ·
verses.22c: μάχαιρα γλῶσσα βασιλέως καὶ οὐ σαρκίνη, ὃς δʼ ἂν παραδοθῇ συντριβήσεται·
verses.22d: ἐὰν γὰρ ὀξυνθῇ ὁ θυμὸς αὐτοῦ, σὺν νεύροις ἀνθρώπους ἀναλίσκει,
verses.22e: καὶ ὀστᾶ ἀνθρώπων κατατρώγει, καὶ συγκαίει ὥσπερ φλὸξ, ὥστε ἄβρωτα εἶναι νεοσσοῖς ἀετῶν·
verses.22f: τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους υἱὲ φοβήθητι, καὶ δεξάμενος αὐτοὺς μετανόει.] Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῖς πιστεύουσι Θεῷ, καὶ παύομαι.
verses.22g: Ἀφρονέστατος γάρ εἰμι ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπων, καὶ φρόνησις ἀνθρώπων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἐμοί.
verses.22h: Θεὸς δεδίδαχέ με σοφίαν, καὶ γνῶσιν ἁγίων ἔγνωκα.
verses.22i: Τίς ἀνέβη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ κατέβη; τίς συνήγαγεν ἀνέμους ἐν κόλπῳ; τίς συνέστρεψεν ὕδωρ ἐν ἱματίῳ; τίς ἐκράτησε πάντων τῶν ἄκρων τῆς γῆς; τί ὄνομα αὐτῷ; ἢ τί ὄνομα τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτοῦ;
verses.22k: Πάντες γὰρ λόγοι Θεοῦ πεπυρωμένοι, ὑπερασπίζει δὲ αὐτὸς τῶν εὐλαβουμένων αὐτόν.
verses.22l: Μὴ προσθῇς τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ ἐλέγξῃ σε, καὶ ψευδὴς γένῃ.
verses.22m: Δύο αἰτοῦμαι παρὰ σοῦ, μὴ ἀφέλῃς μου χάριν πρὸ τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν με.
verses.22n: Μάταιον λόγον καὶ ψευδῆ μακράν μου ποίησον, πλοῦτον δὲ καὶ πενίαν μή μοι δῷς, σύνταξον δέ μοι τὰ δέοντα καὶ τὰ αὐτάρκη·
verses.22o: Ἵνα μὴ πλησθεὶς ψευδὴς γένωμαι, καὶ εἴπω, τίς με ὁρᾷ; ἢ πενηθεὶς κλέψω, καὶ ὀμόσω τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ.
verses.22p: Μὴ παραδῷς οἰκέτην εἰς χεῖρας δεσπότου, μήποτε καταράσηταί σε καὶ ἀφανισθῇς.
verses.22q: Ἔκγονον κακὸν πατέρα καταρᾶται, τὴς δὲ μητέρα οὐκ εὐλογεῖ.
verses.22r: Ἔκγονον κακὸν δίκαιον ἑαυτὸν κρίνει, τὴν δʼ ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀπένιψεν.
verses.22s: Ἔκγονον κακὸν ὑψηλοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχει, τοῖς δὲ βλεφάροις αὐτοῦ ἐπαίρεται.
verses.22t: Ἔκγονον κακὸν μαχαίρας τοὺς ὀδόντας ἔχει, καὶ τὰς μύλας, τομίδας, ὥστε ἀναλίσκειν καὶ κατεσθίειν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, καὶ τοὺς πένητας αὐτῶν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων.
verses.23: Ταῦτα δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν τοῖς σοφοῖς ἐπιγινώσκειν· αἰδεῖσθαι πρόσωπον ἐν κρίσει οὐ καλόν.
verses.24: Ὁ εἰπὼν τὸν ἀσεβῆ, δίκαιός ἐστιν, ἐπικατάρατος λαοῖς ἔσται καὶ μισητὸς εἰς ἔθνη.
verses.25: Οἱ δὲ ἐλέγχοντες βελτίους φανοῦνται, ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς δὲ ἥξει εὐλογία·
verses.26: χείλη δὲ φιλήσουσιν ἀποκρινόμενα λόγους ἀγαθούς.
verses.27: Ἑτοίμαζε εἰς τὴν ἔξοδον τὰ ἔργα σου, καὶ παρασκευάζου εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν, καὶ πορεύου κατόπισθέν μου, καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσεις τὸν οἶκόν σου.
verses.28: Μὴ ἴσθι ψευδὴς μάρτυς ἐπὶ σὸν πολίτην, μηδὲ πλατύνου σοῖς χείλεσι.
verses.29: Μὴ εἴπῃς, ὃν τρόπον ἐχρήσατό μοι, χρήσομαι αὐτῷ, τίσομαι δὲ αὐτὸν ἅ με ἠδίκησεν.
verses.30: Ὥσπερ γεώργιον ἀνὴρ ἄφρων, καὶ ὥσπερ ἀμπελὼν ἄνθρωπος ἐνδεὴς φρενῶν.
verses.31: Ἐὰν ἀφῇς αὐτὸν, χερσωθήσεται καὶ χορτομανήσει ὅλος, καὶ γίνεται ἐκλελειμμένος, οἱ δὲ φραγμοὶ τῶν λίθων αὐτοῦ κατασκάπτονται.
verses.32: Ὕστερον ἐγὼ μετενόησα, ἐπέβλεψα τοῦ ἐκλέξασθαι παιδείαν.
verses.33: Ὀλίγον νυστάζω, ὀλίγον δὲ καθυπνῶ, ὀλίγον δὲ ἐναγκαλίζομαι χερσὶ στήθη.
verses.34: Ἐὰν δὲ τοῦτο ποιῇς, ἥξει προπορευομένη ἡ πενία σου, καὶ ἡ ἔνδειά σου ὥσπερ ἀγαθὸς δρομεύς.
verses.35: Τῇ βδέλλῃ τρεῖς θυγατέρες ἦσαν ἀγαπήσει ἀγαπώμεναι, καὶ αἱ τρεῖς αὗται οὐκ ἐνεπίμπλασαν αὐτὴν, καὶ ἡ τετάρτη οὐκ ἠρκέσθη εἰπεῖν, ἱκανόν.
verses.36: Ἄδης καὶ ἔρως γυναικὸς, καὶ γῆ οὐκ ἐμπιπλαμένη ὕδατος, καὶ ὕδωρ καὶ πῦρ οὐ μὴ εἴπωσιν, ἀρκεῖ.
verses.37: Ὀφθαλμὸν καταγελῶντα πατρὸς, καὶ ἀτιμάζοντα γῆρας μητρὸς, ἐκκόψαισαν αὐτὸν κόρακες ἐκ τῶν φαράγγων, καὶ καταφάγοισαν αὐτὸν νεοσσοὶ ἀετῶν.
verses.38: Τρία δέ ἐστιν ἀδύνατά μοι νοῆσαι, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκω·
verses.39: Ἴχνη ἀετοῦ πετομένου, καὶ ὁδοὺς ὄφεως ἐπὶ πέτρας, καὶ τρίβους νηὸς ποντοπορούσης, καὶ ὁδοὺς ἀνδρὸς ἐν νεότητι.
verses.40: Τοιαύτη ὁδὸς γυναικὸς μοιχαλίδος, ἣ ὅτʼ ἂν πράξῃ ἀπονιψαμένη, οὐδέν φησι πεπραχέναι ἄτοπον.
verses.41: Διὰ τριῶν σείεται ἡ γῆ, τὸ δὲ τέταρτον οὐ δύναται φέρειν·
verses.42: Ἐὰν οἰκέτης βασιλεύσῃ, καὶ ἄφρων πλησθῇ σιτίων,
verses.43: καὶ οἰκέτις ἐὰν ἐκβάλῃ τὴν ἑαυτῆς κυρίαν, καὶ μισητὴ γυνὴ ἐὰν τύχῃ ἀνδρὸς ἀγαθοῦ.
verses.44: Τέσσαρα δὲ ἐλάχιστα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ταῦτα δέ ἐστι σοφώτερα τῶν σοφῶν·
verses.45: Οἱ μύρμηκες οἷς μή ἐστιν ἰσχὺς, καὶ ἑτοιμάζονται θέρους τὴν τροφήν·
verses.46: Καὶ οἱ χοιρογρύλλιοι ἔθνος οὐκ ἰσχυρὸν, οἳ ἐποιήσαντο ἐν πέτραις τοὺς ἑαυτῶν οἴκους·
verses.47: Ἀβασίλευτόν ἐστιν ἡ ἀκρὶς, καὶ στρατεύει ἀφʼ ἑνὸς κελεύσματος εὐτάκτως·
verses.48: Καὶ καλαβώτης χερσὶν ἐρειδόμενος, καὶ εὐάλωτος ὢν, κατοικεῖ ἐν ὀχυρώμασι βασιλέων.
verses.49: Τρία δέ ἐστιν ἃ εὐόδως πορεύεται, καὶ τέταρτον ὃ καλῶς διαβαίνει·
verses.50: Σκύμνος λέοντος ἰσχυρότερος κτηνῶν, ὃς οὐκ ἀποστρέφεται, οὐδὲ καταπτήσσει κτῆνος·
verses.51: Καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐμπεριπατῶν θηλείαις εὔψυχος, καὶ τράγος ἡγούμενος αἰπολίου, καὶ βασιλεὺς δημηγορῶν ἐν ἔθνει.
verses.52: Ἐὰν πρόῃ σεαυτὸν ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ, καὶ ἐκτείνῃς τὴν χεῖρά σου μετὰ μάχης, ἀτιμασθήσῃ.
verses.53: Ἄμελγε γάλα, καὶ ἔσται βούτυρον· ἐὰν δὲ ἐκπιέζῃς μυκτῆρας ἐξελεύσεται αἷμα, ἐὰν δὲ ἐξέλκῃς λόγους, ἐξελεύσονται κρίσεις καὶ μάχαι.
verses.54: Οἱ ἐμοὶ λόγοι εἴρηνται ὑπὸ Θεοῦ, βασιλέως χρηματισμὸς, ὃν ἐπαίδευσεν ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ.
verses.55: Τί τέκνον τηρήσεις; τί; ῥήσεις Θεοῦ· πρωτογενὲς σοὶ λέγω υἱέ· τί τέκνον ἐμῆς κοιλίας; τί τέκνον ἐμῶν εὐχῶν;
verses.56: Μὴ δῷς γυναιξὶ σὸν πλοῦτον, καὶ τὸν σὸν νοῦν καὶ βίον εἰς ὑστεροβουλίαν·
verses.57: μετὰ βουλῆς πάντα ποίει, μετὰ βουλῆς οἰνοπότει. Οἱ δυνάσται θυμώδεις εἰσὶν, οἶνον δὲ μὴ πινέτωσαν,
verses.58: ἵνα μὴ πιόντες ἐπιλάθωνται τῆς σοφίας, καὶ ὀρθὰ κρῖναι οὐ μὴ δύνωνται τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς.
verses.59: Δίδοτε μέθην τοῖς ἐν λύπαις, καὶ οἶνον πίνειν τοῖς ἐν ὀδύναις,
verses.60: ἵνα ἐπιλάθωνται τῆς πενίας, καὶ τῶν πόνων μὴ μνησθῶσιν ἔτι.
verses.61: Ἄνοιγε σὸν στόμα λόγῳ Θεοῦ, καὶ κρίνε πάντας ὑγιῶς.
verses.62: Ἄνοιγε σὸν στόμα καὶ κρίνε δικαίως, διάκρινε δὲ πένητα καὶ ἀσθενῆ.

verses.1: As a rush of water, so is the king's heart in God's hand: he turns it whithersoever he may desire to point out.
verses.2: Every man seems to himself righteous; but the Lord directs the hearts.
verses.3: To do justly and to speak truth, are more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices.
verses.4: A high-minded man is stout-hearted in his pride; and the lamp of the wicked is sin.
verses.6: He that gathers treasures with a lying tongue pursues vanity on to the snares of death.
verses.7: Destruction shall lodge with the ungodly; for they refuse to do justly.
verses.8: To the froward God sends froward ways; for his works are pure and right.
verses.9: It is better to dwell in a corner on the house-top, than in plastered rooms with unrighteousness, and in an open house.
verses.10: The soul of the ungodly shall not be pitied by any man.
verses.11: When an intemperate man is punished the simple becomes wiser: and a wise man understanding will receive knowledge.
verses.12: A righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly: and despises the ungodly for their wickedness.
verses.13: He that stops his ears from hearing the poor, himself also shall cry, and there shall be none to hear him.
verses.14: A secret gift calms anger: but he that forbears to give stirs up strong wrath.
verses.15: It is the joy of the righteous to do judgment: but a holy man is abominable with evil-doers.
verses.16: A man that wanders out of the way of righteousness, shall rest in the congregation of giants.
verses.17: A poor man loves mirth, loving wine and oil in abundance;
verses.18: and a transgressor is the abomination of a righteous man.
verses.19: It is better to dwell in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and talkative and passionate woman.
verses.20: A desirable treasure will rest on the mouth of the wise; but foolish men will swallow it up.
verses.21: The way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory.
verses.22: A wise man assaults strong cities, and demolishes the fortress in which the ungodly trusted.
verses.23: He that keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from trouble.
verses.24: A bold and self-willed and insolent man is called a pest: and he that remembers injuries is a transgressor.
verses.25: Desires kill the sluggard; for his hands do not choose to do anything.
verses.26: An ungodly man entertains evil desires all the day: but the righteous is unsparingly merciful and compassionate.
verses.27: The sacrifices of the ungodly are abomination to the Lord, for they offer them wickedly.
verses.28: A false witness shall perish; but an obedient man will speak cautiously.
verses.29: An ungodly man impudently withstands with his face; but the upright man himself understands his ways.
verses.30: There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel against the ungodly.
verses.31: A horse is prepared for the day of battle; but help is of the Lord.

verses.1: Manasses was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Apsiba.
verses.2: And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel.
verses.3: And he built again the high places, which Ezekias his father had demolished; and set up an altar to Baal, and made groves as Achaab king of Israel made them; and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
verses.4: And he built an altar in the house of the Lord, whereas he had said, In Jerusalem I will place my name.
verses.5: And he built an altar to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.6: And he caused his sons to pass through the fire, and used divination and auspices, and made groves, and multiplied wizards, so as to do that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.
verses.7: And he set up the graven image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David, and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I even place my name for ever.
verses.8: And I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, even of those who shall keep all that I commanded, according to all the commandments which my servant Moses commanded them.
verses.9: But they hearkened not; and Manasses led them astray to do evil in the sight of the Lord, beyond the nations whom the Lord utterly destroyed from before the children of Israel.
verses.10: And the Lord spoke by his servants the prophets, saying,
verses.11: Forasmuch as Manasses the king of Juda has wrought all these evil abominations, beyond all that the Amorite did, who lived before him, and has led Juda also into sin by their idols,
verses.12: it shall not be so. Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Behold, I bring calamities upon Jerusalem and Juda, so that both the ears of every one that hears shall tingle.
verses.13: And I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Achaab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a jar is wiped, and turned upside down in the wiping.
verses.14: And I will reject the remnant of my inheritance, and will deliver them into the hands of their enemies; and they shall be for a plunder and for a spoil to all their enemies:
verses.15: forasmuch as they have done wickedly in my sight, and have provoked me from the day that I brought out their fathers out of Egypt, even until this day.
verses.16: Moreover Manasses shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem with it from one end to the other, beside his sins with which he caused Juda to sin, in doing evil in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.17: And the rest of the acts of Manasses, and all that he did, and his sin which he sinned, are not these things written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda?
verses.18: And Manasses slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his house, even in the garden of Oza: and Amos his son reigned in his stead.
verses.19: Twenty and two years old was Amos when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Mesollam, daughter of Arus of Jeteba.
verses.20: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as Manasses his father did.
verses.21: And he walked in all the way in which his father walked, and served the idols which his father served, and worshipped them.
verses.22: And he forsook the Lord God of his fathers, and walked not in the way of the Lord.
verses.23: And the servants of Amos conspired against him, and slew the king in his house.
verses.24: And the people of the land slew all that had conspired against king Amos; and the people of the land made Josias his son king in his room.
verses.25: And the rest of the acts of Amos, even all that he did, behold, are not these written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Juda?
verses.26: And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Oza: and Josias his son reigned in his stead.

verses.1: For the end. Destroy not: by David for a memorial, when Saul sent, and watched his house to kill him.
verses.2: Deliver me from mine enemies, O God; and ransom me from those that rise up against me.
verses.3: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, and save me from bloody men.
verses.4: For, behold, they have hunted after my soul; violent men have set upon me: neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord.
verses.5: Without iniquity I ran and directed my course aright: awake to help me, and behold.
verses.6: And thou, Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, draw nigh to visit all the heathen; pity not any that work iniquity. Pause.
verses.7: They shall return at evening, and hunger like a dog, and go round about the city.
verses.8: Behold, they shall utter a voice with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips; for who, say they, has heard?
verses.9: But thou, Lord, wilt laugh them to scorn; thou wilt utterly set at nought all the heathen.
verses.10: I will keep my strength, looking to thee; for thou, O God, art my helper.
verses.11: As for my God, his mercy shall go before me: my God will shew me vengeance on mine enemies.
verses.12: Slay them not, lest they forget thy law; scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord, my defender.
verses.13: For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips, let them be even taken in their pride.
verses.14: And for their cursing and falsehood shall utter destruction be denounced: they shall fall by the wrath of utter destruction, and shall not be; so shall they know that the God of Jacob is Lord of the ends of the earth. Pause.
verses.15: They shall return at evening, and be hungry as a dog, and go round about the city.
verses.16: They shall be scattered hither and thither for meat; and if they be not satisfied, they shall even murmur.
verses.17: But I will sing to thy strength, and in the morning will I exult in thy mercy; for thou hast been my supporter, and my refuge in the day of mine affliction.
verses.18: Thou art my helper; to thee, my God, will I sing; thou art my supporter, O my God, and my mercy.

verses.1: So they brought in the ark of God, and set it in the midst of the tabernacle which David pitched for it; and they offered whole-burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before God.
verses.2: And David finished offering up whole-burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord.
verses.3: And he divided to every man of Israel (both men and women), to every man one baker's loaf, and a cake.
verses.4: And he appointed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, Levites to minister and lift up the voice, and to give thanks and praise the Lord God of Israel:
verses.5: Asaph was the chief, and next to him Zacharias, Jeiel, Semiramoth, and Jeiel, Mattathias, Eliab, and Banæas, and Abdedom: and Jeiel sounding with musical instruments, lutes and harps, and Asaph with cymbals:
verses.6: and Banæas and Oziel the priests sounding continually with trumpets before the ark of the covenant of God in that day.
verses.7: Then David first gave orders to praise the Lord by the hand of Asaph and his brethren.
verses.8: Song. Give thanks to the Lord, call upon him by his name, make known his designs among the people.
verses.9: Sing songs to him, and sing hymns to him, relate to all people his wonderful deeds, which the Lord has wrought.
verses.10: Praise his holy name, the heart that seeks his pleasure shall rejoice.
verses.11: Seek the Lord and be strong, seek his face continually.
verses.12: Remember his wonderful works which he has wrought, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth;
verses.13: ye seed of Israel his servants, ye seed of Jacob his chosen ones.
verses.14: He is the Lord our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
verses.15: Let us remember his covenant for ever, his word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
verses.16: which he covenanted with Abraham, and his oath sworn to Isaac.
verses.17: He confirmed it to Jacob for an ordinance, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
verses.18: saying, To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, the line of your inheritance:
verses.19: when they were few in number, when they were but little, and dwelt as strangers in it;
verses.20: and went from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
verses.21: He suffered not a man to oppress them, and he reproved kings for their sakes,
verses.22: saying, Touch not my anointed ones, and deal not wrongfully with my prophets.
verses.23: Sing ye to the Lord, all the earth; proclaim his salvation from day to day.
verses.23a: Declare among the nations his glory, his wondrous deeds among all peoples.
verses.25: For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.26: For all the gods of the nations are idols; but our God made the heavens.
verses.27: Glory and praise are in his presence; strength and rejoicing are in his place.
verses.28: Give to the Lord, ye families of the nations, give to the Lord glory and strength.
verses.29: Give to the Lord the glory belonging to his name: take gifts and offer them before him; and worship the Lord in his holy courts.
verses.30: Let the whole earth fear before him; let the earth be established, and not be moved.
verses.31: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; and let them say among the nations, The Lord reigns.
verses.32: The sea with its fulness shall resound and the tree of the field, and all things in it.
verses.33: Then shall the trees of the wood rejoice before the Lord, for he is come to judge the earth.
verses.34: Give thanks to the Lord, for it is good, for his mercy is for ever.
verses.35: And say ye, Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather us, and rescue us from among the heathen, that we may praise thy holy name, and glory in thy praises.
verses.36: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting and to everlasting: And all the people shall say, Amen. So they praised the Lord.
verses.37: And they left there Asaph and his brethren before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to minister before the ark continually, according to the service of each day: from day to day.
verses.38: And Abdedom and his brethren were sixty and eight; and Abdedom the son of Idithun, and Osa, were to be door-keepers.
verses.39: And they appointed Sadoc the priest, and his brethren the priests, before the tabernacle of the Lord in the high place in Gabaon,
verses.40: to offer up whole-burnt-offerings to the Lord on the altar of whole-burnt-offerings continually morning and evening, and according to all things written in the law of the Lord, which he commanded the children of Israel by Moses the servant of God.
verses.41: And with him were Æman and Idithun, and the rest chosen out by name to praise the Lord, for his mercy endures for ever.
verses.42: And with them there were trumpets and cymbals to sound aloud, and musical instruments for the songs of God: and the sons of Idithun were at the gate.
verses.43: And all the people went every one to his home: and David returned to bless his house.

verses.1: My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God; my mouth is enlarged over my enemies, I have rejoiced in thy salvation.
verses.2: For there is none holy as the Lord, and there is none righteous as our God: there is none holy beside thee.
verses.3: Boast not, and utter not high things; let not high-sounding words come out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and God prepares his own designs.
verses.4: The bow of the mighty has waxed feeble, and the weak have girded themselves with strength.
verses.5: They that were full of bread are brought low; and the hungry have forsaken the land; for the barren has born seven, and she that abounded in children has waxed feeble.
verses.6: The Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to the grave, and brings up.
verses.7: The Lord makes poor, and makes rich; he brings low, and lifts up.
verses.8: He lifts up the poor from the earth, and raises the needy from the dunghill; to seat him with the princes of the people, and causing them to inherit the throne of glory:
verses.9: granting his petition to him that prays; and he blesses the years of the righteous, for by strength cannot man prevail.
verses.10: The Lord will weaken his adversary; the Lord is holy. Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor let the mighty man boast in his strength, and let not the rich man boast in his wealth; but let him that boasts boast in this, to understand and know the Lord, and to execute judgment and justice in the midst of the earth. The Lord has gone up to the heavens, and has thundered: he will judge the extremities of the earth, and he gives strength to our kings, and will exalt the horn of his Christ. And she left him there before the Lord,
verses.11: and departed to Armathaim: and the child ministered in the presence of the Lord before Heli the priest.
verses.12: And the sons of Heli the priest were evil sons, not knowing the Lord.
verses.13: And the priest's claim from every one of the people that sacrificed was this: the servant of the priest came when the flesh was in seething, and a flesh-hook of three teeth was in his hand.
verses.14: And he struck it into the great caldron, or into the brazen vessel, or into the pot, and whatever came up with the flesh-hook, the priest took for himself: so they did to all Israel that came to sacrifice to the Lord in Selom.
verses.15: And before the fat was burnt for a sweet savour, the servant of the priest would come, and say to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest, and I will by no means take of thee sodden flesh out of the caldron.
verses.16: And if the man that sacrificed said, First let the fat be burned, as it is fit, and take for thyself of all things which thy soul desires: then he would say, Nay, for thou shalt give it me now; and if not, I will take it by force.
verses.17: So the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord, for they set at nought the offering of the Lord.
verses.18: And Samuel ministered before the Lord, a child girt with a linen ephod.
verses.19: And his mother made him a little doublet, and brought it to him from year to year, in her going up in company with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
verses.20: And Heli blessed Helcana and his wife, saying, The Lord recompense to thee seed of this woman, in return for the loan which thou hast lent to the Lord: and the man returned to his place.
verses.21: And the Lord visited Anna, and she bore yet three sons, and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the Lord.
verses.22: And Heli was very old, and he heard what his sons did to the children of Israel.
verses.23: And he said to them, Why do ye according to this thing, which I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord?
verses.24: Nay my sons, for the report which I hear is not good; do not so, for the reports which I hear are not good, so that the people do not serve God.
verses.25: If a man should at all sin against another, then shall they pray for him to the Lord; but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall intreat for him? But they hearkened not to the voice of their father, because the Lord would by all means destroy them.
verses.26: And the child Samuel advanced, and was in favour with God and with men.
verses.27: And a man of God came to Heli, and said, Thus says the Lord, I plainly revealed myself to the house of thy father, when they were servants in Egypt to the house of Pharao.
verses.28: And I chose the house of thy father out of all the tribes of Israel to minister to me in the priest's office, to go up to my altar, and to burn incense, and to wear an ephod. And I gave to the house of thy father all the offerings by fire of the children of Israel for food.
verses.29: And wherefore hast thou looked upon my incense-offering and my meat-offering with a shameless eye, and hast honoured thy sons above me, so that they should bless themselves with the first-fruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me?
verses.30: Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel, I said, Thy house and the house of thy father shall pass before me for ever: but now the Lord says, That be far from me; for I will only honour them that honour me, and he that sets me at nought shall be despised.
verses.31: Behold, the days come when I will destroy thy seed and the seed of thy father's house.
verses.32: And thou shalt not have an old man in my house for ever.
verses.33: And if I do not destroy a man of thine from my altar, it shall be that his eyes may fail and his soul may perish; and every one that remains in thy house shall fall by the sword of men.
verses.34: And this which shall come upon thy two sons Ophni and Phinees shall be a sign to thee; in one day they shall both die.
verses.35: And I will raise up to myself a faithful priest, who shall do all that is in my heart and in my soul; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before my Christ for ever.
verses.36: And it shall come to pass that he that survives in thy house, shall come to do obeisance before him for a little piece of silver, saying, Put me into one of thy priests' offices to eat bread.

verses.1: And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and the Devil stood on his right hand to resist him. And the Lord said to the Devil,
verses.2: The Lord rebuke thee, O Devil, even the Lord that has chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee: behold! is not this as a brand plucked from the fire?
verses.3: Now Jesus was clothed in filthy raiment, and stood before the angel.
verses.4: And the Lord answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy raiment from him: and he said to him, Behold, I have taken away thine iniquities: and clothe ye him with a long robe,
verses.5: and place a pure mitre upon his head. So they placed a pure mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments: and the angel of the Lord stood by.
verses.6: And the angel of the Lord testified to Jesus, saying,
verses.7: Thus saith the Lord Almighty; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and take heed to my charges, then shalt thou judge my house: and if thou wilt diligently keep my court, then will I give thee men to walk in the midst of these that stand here.
verses.8: Hear now, Jesus the high priest, thou, and thy neighbours that are sitting before thee: for they are diviners, for, behold, I bring forth my servant The Branch.
verses.9: For as for the stone which I have set before the face of Jesus, on the one stone are seven eyes: behold, I am digging a trench, saith the Lord Almighty, and I will search out all the iniquity of that land in one day.
verses.10: In that day, saith the Lord Almighty, ye shall call together every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig-tree.

verses.1: A wise son makes his father glad: but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
verses.2: Treasures shall not profit the lawless: but righteousness shall deliver from death.
verses.3: The Lord will not famish a righteous soul: but he will overthrow the life of the ungodly.
verses.4: Poverty brings a man low: but the hands of the vigorous make rich.
verses.4a: A son who is instructed shall be wise, and shall use the fool for a servant.
verses.5: A wise son is saved from heat: but a lawless son is blighted of the winds in harvest.
verses.6: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but untimely grief shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.
verses.7: The memory of the just is praised; but the name of the ungodly man is extinguished.
verses.8: A wise man in heart will receive commandments; but he that is unguarded in his lips shall be overthrown in his perverseness.
verses.9: He that walks simply, walks confidently; but he that perverts his ways shall be known.
verses.10: He that winks with his eyes deceitfully, procures griefs for men; but he that reproves boldly is a peacemaker.
verses.11: There is a fountain of life in the hand of a righteous man; but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.
verses.12: Hatred stirs up strife; but affection covers all that do not love strife.
verses.13: He that brings forth wisdom from his lips smites the fool with a rod.
verses.14: The wise will hide discretion; but the mouth of the hasty draws near to ruin.
verses.15: The wealth of rich men is a strong city; but poverty is the ruin of the ungodly.
verses.16: The works of the righteous produce life; but the fruits of the ungodly produce sins.
verses.17: Instruction keeps the right ways of life; but instruction unchastened goes astray.
verses.18: Righteous lips cover enmity; but they that utter railings are most foolish.
verses.19: By a multitude of words thou shalt not escape sin; but if thou refrain thy lips thou wilt be prudent.
verses.20: The tongue of the just is tried silver; but the heart of the ungodly shall fail.
verses.21: The lips of the righteous know sublime truths: but the foolish die in want.
verses.22: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; it enriches him, and grief of heart shall not be added to it.
verses.23: A fool does mischief in sport; but wisdom brings forth prudence for a man.
verses.24: The ungodly is engulphed in destruction; but the desire of the righteous is acceptable.
verses.25: When the storm passes by, the ungodly vanishes away; but the righteous turns aside and escapes for ever.
verses.26: As a sour grape is hurtful to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so iniquity hurts those that practise it.
verses.27: The fear of the Lord adds length of days: but the years of the ungodly shall be shortened.
verses.28: Joy rests long with the righteous: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.29: The fear of the Lord is a strong hold of the saints: but ruin comes to them that work wickedness.
verses.30: The righteous shall never fail: but the ungodly shall not dwell in the earth.
verses.31: The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom: but the tongue of the unjust shall perish.
verses.32: The lips of just men drop grace: but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse.

verses.1: And the Ziphites come out of the dry country to Saul to the hill, saying, Behold, David hides himself with us in the hill Echela, opposite Jessemon.
verses.2: And Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him went three thousand men chosen out of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.3: And Saul encamped in the hill of Echela in front of Jessemon, by the way, and David dwelt in the wilderness: and David saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
verses.4: And David sent spies, and ascertained that Saul was come prepared out of Keila.
verses.5: And David arose secretly, and goes into the place where Saul was sleeping, and there was Abenner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul was sleeping in a chariot, and the people had encamped round about him.
verses.6: And David answered and spoke to Abimelech the Chettite, and to Abessa the son of Saruia the brother of Joab, saying, Who will go in with me to Saul into the camp? And Abessa said, I will go in with thee.
verses.7: So David and Abessa go in among the people by night: and behold, Saul was fast asleep in the chariot, and his spear was stuck in the ground near his head, and Abenner and his people slept round about him.
verses.8: And Abessa said to David, The Lord has this day shut up thine enemy into thine hands, and now I will smite him to the earth with the spear to the ground once for all, and I will not smite him again.
verses.9: And David said to Abessa, Do not lay him low, for who shall lift up his hand against the anointed of the Lord, and be guiltless?
verses.10: And David said, As the Lord lives, if the Lord smite him not, or his day come and he die, or he go down to battle and be added to his fathers, do not so.
verses.11: The Lord forbid it me that I should lift up my hand against the anointed of the Lord: and now take, I pray thee, the spear from his bolster, and the pitcher of water, and let us return home.
verses.12: So David took the spear, and the pitcher of water from his bolster, and they went home: and there was no one that saw, and no one that knew, and there was no one that awoke, all being asleep, for a stupor from the Lord had fallen upon them.
verses.13: So David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of a hill afar off, and there was a good distance between them.
verses.14: And David called to the people, and spoke to Abenner, saying, Wilt thou not answer, Abenner? and Abenner answered and said, Who art thou that callest?
verses.15: And David said to Abenner, Art not thou a man? and who is like thee in Israel? Why then dost thou not guard thy lord the king? for one out of the people went in to destroy thy lord the king.
verses.16: And this thing is not good which thou hast done. As the Lord lives, ye are worthy of death, ye who guard your lord the king, the anointed of the Lord: and now behold, I pray you, the spear of the king, and the cruse of water: where are the articles that should be at his head?
verses.17: And Saul recognised the voice of David, and said, Is this thy voice, son David? and David said, I am thy servant, my lord, O king.
verses.18: And he said, Why does my lord thus pursue after his servant? for in what have I sinned? and what unrighteousness has been found in me?
verses.19: And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant. If God stirs thee up against me, let thine offering be acceptable: but if the sons of men, they are cursed before the Lord, for they have cast me out this day so that I should not be established in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.
verses.20: And now let not my blood fall to the ground before the Lord, for the king of Israel has come forth to seek thy life, as the night hawk pursues its prey in the mountains.
verses.21: And Saul said, I have sinned: turn, son David, for I will not hurt thee, because my life was precious in thine eyes; and to-day I have been foolish and have erred exceedingly.
verses.22: And David answered and said, Behold, the spear of the king: let one of the servants come over and take it.
verses.23: And the Lord shall recompense each according to his righteousness and his truth, since the Lord delivered thee this day into my hands, and I would not lift my hand against the Lord's anointed.
verses.24: And, behold, as thy life has been precious this very day in my eyes, so let my life be precious before the Lord, and may he protect me, and deliver me out of all affliction.
verses.25: And Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son; and thou shalt surely do valiantly, and surely prevail. And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

verses.1: Anger slays even wise men; yet a submissive answer turns away wrath: but a grievous word stirs up anger.
verses.2: The tongue of the wise knows what is good: but the mouth of the foolish tells out evil things.
verses.3: The eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good in every place.
verses.4: The wholesome tongue is a tree of life, and he that keeps it shall be filled with understanding.
verses.5: A fool scorns his father's instruction: but he that keeps his commandments is more prudent. In abounding righteousness is great strength: but the ungodly shall utterly perish from the earth.
verses.6: In the houses of the righteous is much strength: but the fruits of the ungodly shall perish.
verses.7: The lips of the wise are bound by discretion: but the hearts of the foolish are not safe.
verses.8: The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord; but the prayers of them that walk honestly are acceptable with him.
verses.9: The ways of an ungodly man are an abomination to the Lord; but he loves those that follow after righteousness.
verses.10: The instruction of the simple is known by them that pass by; but they that hate reproofs die disgracefully.
verses.11: Hell and destruction are manifest to the Lord; how shall not also be the hearts of men?
verses.12: An uninstructed person will not love those that reprove him; neither will he associate with the wise.
verses.13: When the heart rejoices the countenance is cheerful; but when it is in sorrow, the countenance is sad.
verses.14: An upright heart seeks discretion; but the mouth of the uninstructed will experience evils.
verses.15: The eyes of the wicked are always looking for evil things; but the good are always quiet.
verses.16: Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without the fear of the Lord.
verses.17: Better is an entertainment of herbs with friendliness and kindness, than a feast of calves, with enmity.
verses.18: A passionate man stirs up strife; but he that is slow to anger appeases even a rising one.
verses.18a: A man slow to anger will extinguish quarrels; but an ungodly man rather stirs them up.
verses.19: The ways of sluggards are strewn with thorns; but those of the diligent are made smooth.
verses.20: A wise son gladdens his father; but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
verses.21: The ways of a foolish man are void of sense; but a wise man proceeds on his way aright.
verses.22: They that honour not councils put off deliberation; but counsel abides in the hearts of counsellors.
verses.23: A bad man will by no means attend to counsel; neither will he say anything seasonable, or good for the common weal.
verses.24: The thoughts of the wise are ways of life, that he may turn aside and escape from hell.
verses.25: The Lord pulls down the houses of scorners; but he establishes the border of the widow.
verses.26: An unrighteous thought is abomination to the Lord; but the sayings of the pure are held in honour.
verses.27: A receiver of bribes destroys himself; but he that hates the receiving of bribes is safe.
verses.27a: [By alms and by faithful dealings sins are purged away;] but by the fear of the Lord every one departs from evil.
verses.28: The hearts of the righteous meditate faithfulness; but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things.
verses.28a: The ways of righteous men are acceptable with the Lord; and through them even enemies become friends.
verses.29: God is far from the ungodly; but he hearkens to the prayers of the righteous.
verses.29a: Better are small receipts with righteousness, than abundant fruits with unrighteousness.
verses.29b: Let the heart of a man think justly, that his steps may be rightly ordered of God.
verses.30: The eye that sees rightly rejoices the heart; and a good report fattens the bones.
verses.32: He that rejects instruction hates himself; but he that minds reproofs loves his soul.
verses.33: The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom; and the highest honour will correspond therewith.

verses.1: And the word of the Lord came to me, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying,
verses.2: Son of man, write for thyself daily from this day, on which the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem, even from this day.
verses.3: And speak a parable to the provoking house, and thou shalt say to them, Thus saith the Lord; Set on the caldron, and pour water into it:
verses.4: and put the pieces into it, every prime piece, the leg and shoulder taken off from the bones,
verses.5: which are taken from choice cattle, and burn the bones under them: her bones are boiled and cooked in the midst of her.
verses.6: Therefore thus saith the Lord; O bloody city, the caldron in which there is scum, and the scum has not gone out of, she has brought it forth piece by piece, no lot has fallen upon it.
verses.7: For her blood is in the midst of her; I have set it upon a smooth rock: I have not poured it out upon the earth, so that the earth should cover it;
verses.8: that my wrath should come up for complete vengeance to be taken: I set her blood upon a smooth rock, so as not to cover it.
verses.9: Therefore thus saith the Lord, I will also make the firebrand great,
verses.10: and I will multiply the wood, and kindle the fire, that the flesh may be consumed, and the liquor boiled away;
verses.11: and that it may stand upon the coals, that her brass may be thoroughly heated, and be melted in the midst of her filthiness, and her scum may be consumed,
verses.12: and her abundant scum may not come forth of her.
verses.13: Her scum shall become shameful, because thou didst defile thyself: and what if thou shalt be purged no more until I have accomplished my wrath?
verses.14: I the Lord have spoken; and it shall come, and I will do it; I will not delay, neither will I have any mercy: I will judge thee, saith the Lord, according to thy ways, and according to thy devices: therefore will I judge thee according to thy bloodshed, and according to thy devices will I judge thee, thou unclean, notorious, and abundantly provoking one.
verses.15: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.16: Son of man, behold I take from thee the desire of thine eyes by violence: thou shalt not lament, neither shalt thou weep.
verses.17: Thou shalt groan for blood, and have mourning upon thy loins; thy hair shall not be braided upon thee, and thy sandals shall be on thy feet; thou shalt in no wise be comforted by their lips, and thou shalt not eat the bread of men.
verses.18: And I spoke to the people in the morning, as he commanded me in the evening, and I did in the morning as it was commanded me.
verses.19: And the people said to me, Wilt thou not tell us what these things are that thou doest?
verses.20: Then I said to them, The word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.21: Say to the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the boast of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and for which your souls are concerned; and your sons and your daughters, whom ye have left, shall fall by the sword.
verses.22: And ye shall do as I have done: ye shall not be comforted at their mouth, and ye shall not eat the bread of men.
verses.23: And your hair shall be upon your head, and your shoes on your feet: neither shall ye at all lament or weep; but ye shall pine away in your iniquities, and shall comfort every one his brother.
verses.24: And Jezekiel shall be for a sign to you: according to all that I have done shall ye do, when these things shall come; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.25: And thou, son of man, shall it not be in the day when I take their strength from them, the pride of their boasting, the desires of their eyes, and the pride of their soul, their sons and their daughters,
verses.26: that in that day he that escapes shall come to thee, to tell it thee in thine ears?
verses.27: In that day thy mouth shall be opened to him that escapes; thou shalt speak, and shalt be no longer dumb: and thou shalt be for a sign to them, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

verses.1: And the Philistines gather all their armies to Aphec, and Israel encamped in Aendor, which is in Jezrael.
verses.2: And the lords of the Philistines went on by hundreds and thousands, and David and his men went on in the rear with Anchus.
verses.3: And the lords of the Philistines said, Who are these that pass by? And Anchus said to the captains of the Philistines, Is not this David the servant of Saul king of Israel? he has been with us some time, even this second year, and I have not found any fault in him from the day that he attached himself to me even until this day.
verses.4: And the captains of the Philistines were displeased at him, and they say to him, Send the man away, and let him return to his place, where thou didst set him; and let him not come with us to the war, and let him not be a traitor in the camp: and wherewith will he be reconciled to his master? will it not be with the heads of those men?
verses.5: Is not this David whom they celebrated in dances, saying, Saul has smitten his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
verses.6: And Anchus called David, and said to him, As the Lord lives, thou art right and approved in my eyes, and so is thy going out and thy coming in with me in the army, and I have not found any evil to charge against thee from the day that thou camest to me until this day: but thou art not approved in the eyes of the lords.
verses.7: Now then return and go in peace, thus thou shalt not do evil in the sight of the lords of the Philistines.
verses.8: And David said to Anchus, What have I done to thee? and what hast thou found in thy servant from the first day that I was before thee even until this day, that I should not come and war against the enemies of the lord my king?
verses.9: And Anchus answered David, I know that thou art good in my eyes, but the lords of the Philistines say, He shall not come with us to the war.
verses.10: Now then rise up early in the morning, thou and the servants of thy lord that are come with thee, and go to the place where I appointed you, and entertain no evil thought in thy heart, for thou art good in my sight: and rise early for your journey when it is light, and depart.
verses.11: So David arose early, he and his men, to depart and guard the land of the Philistines: and the Philistines went up to Jezrael to battle.

verses.1: Wise women build houses: but a foolish one digs hers down with her hands.
verses.2: He that walks uprightly fears the Lord; but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonoured.
verses.3: Out of the mouth of fools comes a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them.
verses.4: Where no oxen are, the cribs are clean; but where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is apparent.
verses.5: A faithful witness does not lie; but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods.
verses.6: Thou shalt seek wisdom with bad men, and shalt not find it; but discretion is easily available with the prudent.
verses.7: All things are adverse to a foolish man; but wise lips are the weapons of discretion.
verses.8: The wisdom of the prudent will understand their ways; but the folly of fools leads astray.
verses.9: The houses of transgressors will need purification; but the houses of the just are acceptable.
verses.10: If a man's mind is intelligent, his soul is sorrowful; and when he rejoices, he has no fellowship with pride.
verses.11: The houses of ungodly men shall be utterly destroyed; but the tabernacles of them that walk uprightly shall stand.
verses.12: There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depth of hell.
verses.13: Grief mingles not with mirth; and joy in the end comes to grief.
verses.14: A stout-hearted man shall be filled with his own ways; and a good man with his own thoughts.
verses.15: The simple believes every word: but the prudent man betakes himself to after-thought.
verses.16: A wise man fears, and departs from evil; but the fool trusts in himself, and joins himself with the transgressor.
verses.17: A passionate man acts inconsiderately; but a sensible man bears up under many things.
verses.18: Fools shall have mischief for their portion; but the prudent shall take fast hold of understanding.
verses.19: Evil men shall fall before the good; and the ungodly shall attend at the gates of the righteous.
verses.20: Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many.
verses.21: He that dishonours the needy sins: but he that has pity on the poor is most blessed.
verses.22: They that go astray devise evils: but the good devise mercy and truth. The framers of evil do not understand mercy and truth: but compassion and faithfulness are with the framers of good.
verses.23: With every one who is careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in want.
verses.24: A prudent man is the crown of the wise: but the occupation of fools is evil.
verses.25: A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evil: but a deceitful man kindles falsehoods.
verses.26: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and he leaves his children a support.
verses.27: The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causes men to turn aside from the snare of death.
verses.28: In a populous nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of people is the ruin of a prince.
verses.29: A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish.
verses.30: A meek-spirited man is a healer of the heart: but a sensitive heart is a corruption of the bones.
verses.31: He that oppresses the needy provokes his Maker: but he that honours him has pity upon the poor.
verses.32: The ungodly shall be driven away in his wickedness: but he who is secure in his own holiness is just.
verses.33: There is wisdom in the good heart of a man: but in the heart of fools it is not discerned.
verses.34: Righteousness exalts a nation: but sins diminish tribes.
verses.35: An understanding servant is acceptable to a king; and by his good behaviour he removes disgrace.

verses.1: And the ark was seven months in the country of the Philistines, and their land brought forth swarms of mice.
verses.2: And the Philistines call their priests, and their prophets, and their enchanters, saying, What shall we do to the ark of the Lord? teach us wherewith we shall send it away to its place.
verses.3: And they said, If ye send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, do not on any account send it away empty, but by all means render to it an offering for the plague; and then shall ye be healed, and an atonement shall be made for you: should not his hand be thus stayed from off you?
verses.4: And they say, What is the offering for the plague which we shall return to it? and they said,
verses.5: According to the number of the lords of the Philistines, five golden emerods, for the plague was on you, and on your rulers, and on the people; and golden mice, the likeness of the mice that destroy your land: and ye shall give glory to the Lord, that he may lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.
verses.6: And why do ye harden your hearts, as Egypt and Pharao hardened their hearts? was it not so when he mocked them, that they let the people go, and they departed?
verses.7: And now take wood and make a new waggon, and take two cows, that have calved for the first time, without their calves; and do ye yoke the cows to the waggon, and lead away the calves from behind them home.
verses.8: And ye shall take the ark and put it on the waggon; and ye shall restore to it the golden articles for the trespass-offering in a coffer by the side of it: and ye shall let it go, and send it away, and ye shall depart.
verses.9: And ye shall see, if it shall go the way of its coasts along by Bæthsamys, he has brought upon us this great affliction; and if not, then shall we know that his hand has not touched us, but this is a chance which has happened to us.
verses.10: And the Philistines did so; and they took two cows that had calved for the first time, and yoked them to the waggon, and shut up their calves at home.
verses.11: And they set the ark of the Lord, and the coffer, and the golden mice, on the waggon.
verses.12: And the cows went straight on the way to the way of Bæthsamys, they went along one track; and laboured, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left, and the lords of the Philistines went after it as far as the coasts of Bæthsamys.
verses.13: And the men of Bæthsamys were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark of the Lord, and rejoiced to meet it.
verses.14: And the waggon entered into the field of Osee, which was in Bæthsamys, and they set there by it a great stone; and they split the wood of the waggon, and offered up the cows for a whole-burnt-offering to the Lord.
verses.15: And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord, and the coffer with it, and the golden articles upon it, and placed them on the great stone, and the men of Bæthsamys offered whole-burnt-offerings and meat-offerings on that day to the Lord.
verses.16: And the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon in that day.
verses.17: And these are the golden emerods which the lords of the Philistines gave as a trespass-offering to the Lord; for Azotus one, for Gaza one, for Ascalon one, for Geth one, for Accaron one.
verses.18: And the golden mice according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines, belonging to the five lords, from the fenced city to the village of the Pherezite, and to the great stone, on which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that was in the field of Osee the Bæthsamysite.
verses.19: And the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Bæthsamys, because they saw the ark of the Lord; and the Lord smote among them seventy men, and fifty thousand men: and the people mourned, because the Lord had inflicted on the people a very great plague.
verses.20: And the men of Bæthsamys said, Who shall be able to pass before this holy Lord God? and to whom shall the ark of the Lord go up from us?
verses.21: And they send messengers to the inhabitants of Cariathiarim, saying, The Philistines have brought back the ark of the Lord, go down and take it home to yourselves.

verses.1: And it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.2: Son of man, because Sor has said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is crushed: the nations are destroyed: she is turned to me: she that was full is made desolate:
verses.3: therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I am against thee, O Sor, and I will bring up many nations against thee, as the sea comes up with its waves.
verses.4: And they shall cast down the walls of Sor, and shall cast down thy towers: and I will scrape her dust from off her, and make her a bare rock.
verses.5: She shall be in the midst of the sea a place for repairing nets: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord: and it shall be a spoil for the nations.
verses.6: And her daughters which are in the field shall be slain with the sword, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.7: For thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will bring up against thee, O Sor, Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon from the north: he is a king of kings, with horses, and chariots, and horsemen, and a concourse of very many nations.
verses.8: He shall slay thy daughters that are in the field with the sword, and shall set a watch against thee, and build forts around thee, and carry a rampart round against thee, and set up warlike works, and array his spears against thee.
verses.9: He shall cast down with his swords thy walls and thy towers.
verses.10: By reason of the multitude of his horses their dust shall cover thee, and by reason of the sound of his horsemen and the wheels of his chariots thy walls shall be shaken, when he enters into thy gates, as one entering into a city from the plain.
verses.11: With the hoofs of his horses they shall trample all thy streets: he shall slay thy people with the sword, and shall bring down to the ground the support of thy strength.
verses.12: And he shall prey upon thy power, and plunder thy substance, and shall cast down thy walls, and break down thy pleasant houses: and he shall cast thy stones and thy timber and thy dust into the midst of thy sea.
verses.13: And he shall destroy the multitude of thy musicians, and the sound of thy psalteries shall be heard no more.
verses.14: And I will make thee a bare rock: thou shalt be a place to spread nets upon; thou shalt be built no more: for I the Lord have spoken it, saith the Lord.
verses.15: For thus saith the Lord God to Sor; Shall not the isles shake at the sound of thy fall, while the wounded are groaning, while they have drawn a sword in the midst of thee?
verses.16: And all the princes of the nations of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and shall take off their crowns from their heads, and shall take off their embroidered raiment: they shall be utterly amazed; they shall sit upon the ground, and fear their own destruction, and shall groan over thee.
verses.17: And they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and shall say to thee, How art thou destroyed from out of the sea, the renowned city, that brought her terror upon all her inhabitants.
verses.18: And the isles shall be alarmed at the day of thy fall.
verses.19: For thus saith the Lord God; When I shall make the city desolate, as the cities that shall not be inhabited, when I have brought the deep up upon thee,
verses.20: and great waters shall cover thee; and I shall bring thee down to them that go down to the pit, to the people of old time, and shall cause thee to dwell in the depths of the earth, as in everlasting desolation, with them that go down to the pit, that thou mayest not be inhabited, nor stand upon the land of life;
verses.21: I will make thee a destruction, and thou shalt be no more for ever, saith the Lord God.

verses.1: Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace, than a house full of many good things and unjust sacrifices, with strife.
verses.2: A wise servant shall have rule over foolish masters, and shall divide portions among brethren.
verses.3: As silver and gold are tried in a furnace, so are choice hearts with the Lord.
verses.4: A bad man hearkens to the tongue of transgressors: but a righteous man attends not to false lips.
verses.5: He that laughs at the poor provokes him that made him; and he that rejoices at the destruction of another shall not be held guiltless: but he that has compassion shall find mercy.
verses.6: Children's children are the crown of old men; and their fathers are the glory of children.
verses.6a: The faithful has the whole world full of wealth; but the faithless not even a farthing.
verses.7: Faithful lips will not suit a fool; nor lying lips a just man.
verses.8: Instruction is to them that use it a gracious reward: and whithersoever it may turn, it shall prosper.
verses.9: He that conceals injuries seeks love; but he that hates to hide them separates friends and kindred.
verses.10: A threat breaks down the heart of a wise man; but a fool, though scourged, understands not.
verses.11: Every bad man stirs up strifes: but the Lord will send out against him an unmerciful messenger.
verses.12: Care may befall a man of understanding; but fools will meditate evils.
verses.13: Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not be removed from his house.
verses.14: Rightful rule gives power to words; but sedition and strife precede poverty.
verses.15: He that pronounces the unjust just, and the just unjust, is unclean and abominable with God.
verses.16: Why has the fool wealth? for a senseless man will not be able to purchase wisdom.
verses.16a: He that exalts his own house seeks ruin; and he that turns aside from instruction shall fall into mischiefs.
verses.17: Have thou a friend for every time, and let brethren be useful in distress; for on this account are they born.
verses.18: A foolish man applauds and rejoices over himself, as he also that becomes surety would make himself responsible for his own friends.
verses.19: A lover of sin rejoices in strifes;
verses.20: and the hard-hearted man comes not in for good. A man of a changeful tongue will fall into mischiefs;
verses.21: and the heart of a fool is grief to its possessor. A father rejoices not over an uninstructed son; but a wise son gladdens his mother.
verses.22: A glad heart promotes health; but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up.
verses.23: The ways of a man who unjustly receives gifts in his bosom do not prosper; and an ungodly man perverts the ways of righteousness.
verses.24: The countenance of a wise man is sensible; but the eyes of a fool go to the ends of the earth.
verses.25: A foolish son is a cause of anger to his father, and grief to her that bore him.
verses.26: It is not right to punish a righteous man, nor is it holy to plot against righteous princes.
verses.27: He that forbears to utter a hard word is discreet, and a patient man is wise.
verses.28: Wisdom shall be imputed to a fool who asks after wisdom: and he who holds his peace shall seem to be sensible.

verses.1: And the sons of the prophets said to Elisaie, Behold now, the place wherein we dwell before thee is too narrow for us.
verses.2: Let us go, we pray thee, unto Jordan, and take thence every man a beam, and make for ourselves a habitation there.
verses.3: And he said, Go. And one of them said gently, Come with thy servants. And he said, I will go.
verses.4: And he went with them, and they came to Jordan, and began to cut down wood.
verses.5: And behold, one was cutting down a beam, and the axe head fell into the water: and he cried out, Alas! master: and it was hidden.
verses.6: And the man of God said, Where did it fall? and he shewed him the place: and he broke off a stick, and threw it in there, and the iron came to the surface.
verses.7: And he said, Take it up to thyself. And he stretched out his hand, and took it.
verses.8: And the king of Syria was at war with Israel: and he consulted with his servants, saying, I will encamp in such a place.
verses.9: And Elisaie sent to the king of Israel, saying, Take heed that thou pass not by that place, for the Syrians are hidden there.
verses.10: And the king of Israel sent to the place which Elisaie mentioned to him, and saved himself thence not once or twice.
verses.11: And the mind of the king of Syria was very much disturbed concerning this thing; and he called his servants, and said to them, Will ye not tell me who betrays me to the king of Israel?
verses.12: And one of his servants said, Nay, my Lord, O king, for Elisaie the prophet that is in Israel reports to the king of Israel all the words whatsoever thou mayest say in thy bedchamber.
verses.13: And he said, Go, see where this man is, and I will send and take him. And they sent word to him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothaim.
verses.14: And he sent thither horses, and chariots, and a mighty host: and they came by night, and compassed about the city.
verses.15: And the servant of Elisaie rose up early and went out; and, behold, a host compassed the city, and horses and chariots: and the servant said to him, O master, what shall we do?
verses.16: And Elisaie said, Fear not, for they who are with us are more than they that are with them.
verses.17: And Elisaie prayed, and said, Lord, open, I pray thee, the eyes of the servant, and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses, and there were chariots of fire round about Elisaie.
verses.18: And they came down to him; and he prayed to the Lord, and said, Smite, I pray thee, this people with blindness. And he smote them with blindness, according to the word of Elisaie.
verses.19: And Elisaie said to them, This is not the city, and this is not the way: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom ye seek. And he led them away to Samaria.
verses.20: And it came to pass when they entered into Samaria, that Elisaie said, Open, I pray thee, O Lord, their eyes, and let them see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
verses.21: And the king of Israel said to Elisaie, when he saw them, Shall I not verily smite them, my father?
verses.22: And he said, Thou shalt not smite them, unless thou wouldest smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow: set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink, and depart to their master.
verses.23: And he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank: and he dismissed them, and they departed to their master. And the bands of Syria came no longer into the land of Israel.
verses.24: And it came to pass after this, that the son of Ader king of Syria gathered all his army, and went up, and besieged Samaria.
verses.25: And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was valued at fifty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung at five pieces of silver.
verses.26: And the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, and a woman cried to him, saying, Help, my lord, O king.
verses.27: And he said to her, Unless the Lord help thee, whence shall I help thee? from the corn-floor, or from the wine-press?
verses.28: And the king said to her, What is the matter with thee? And the woman said to him, This woman said to me, Give thy son, and we will eat him to-day, and we will eat my son to-morrow.
verses.29: So we boiled my son, and ate him; and I said to her on the second day, Give thy son, and let us eat him: and she has hidden her son.
verses.30: And it came to pass, when the king of Israel heard the words of the woman, that he rent his garments; and he passed by on the wall, and the people saw sackcloth within upon his flesh.
verses.31: And he said, God do so to me and more also, if the head of Elisaie shall stand upon him this day.
verses.32: And Elisaie was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him; and the king sent a man before him: before the messenger came to him, he also said to the elders, Do ye see that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? See, as soon as the messenger shall have come, shut the door, and forcibly detain him at the door: is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?
verses.33: While he was yet speaking with them, behold, a messenger came to him: and he said, Behold, this evil is of the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?

verses.1: Boast not of to-morrow; for thou knowest not what the next day shall bring forth.
verses.2: Let thy neighbour, and not thine own mouth, praise thee; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
verses.3: A stone is heavy, and sand cumbersome; but a fool's wrath is heavier than both.
verses.4: Wrath is merciless, and anger sharp: but envy can bear nothing.
verses.5: Open reproofs are better than secret love.
verses.6: The wounds of a friend are more to be trusted than the spontaneous kisses of an enemy.
verses.7: A full soul scorns honeycombs; but to a hungry soul even bitter things appear sweet.
verses.8: As when a bird flies down from its own nest, so a man is brought into bondage whenever he estranges himself from his own place.
verses.9: The heart delights in ointments and wines and perfumes: but the soul is broken by calamities.
verses.10: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; and when thou art in distress go not into thy brother's house: better is a friend that is near than a brother living far off.
verses.11: Son, be wise, that thy heart may rejoice; and remove thou from thyself reproachful words.
verses.12: A wise man, when evils are approaching, hides himself; but fools pass on, and will be punished.
verses.13: Take away the man's garment, (for a scorner has passed by) whoever lays waste another's goods.
verses.14: Whosoever shall bless a friend in the morning with a loud voice, shall seem to differ nothing from one who curses him.
verses.15: On a stormy day drops of rain drive a man out of his house; so also does a railing woman drive a man out of his own house.
verses.16: The north wind is sharp, but it is called by name propitious.
verses.17: Iron sharpens iron; and a man sharpens his friend's countenance.
verses.18: He that plants a fig-tree shall eat the fruits of it: so he that waits on his own master shall be honoured.
verses.19: As faces are not like other faces, so neither are the thoughts of men.
verses.20: Hell and destruction are not filled; so also are the eyes of men insatiable.
verses.20a: [He that fixes his eye is an abomination to the Lord; and the uninstructed do not restrain their tongue.]
verses.21: Fire is the trial for silver and gold; and a man is tried by the mouth of them that praise him.
verses.21a: The heart of the transgressor seeks after mischiefs; but an upright heart seeks knowledge.
verses.22: Though thou scourge a fool, disgracing him in the midst of the council, thou wilt still in no wise remove his folly from him.
verses.23: Do thou thoroughly know the number of thy flock, and pay attention to thine herds.
verses.24: For a man has not strength and power for ever; neither does he transmit it from generation to generation.
verses.25: Take care of the herbage in the field, and thou shalt cut grass, and gather the mountain hay;
verses.26: that thou mayest have wool of sheep for clothing: pay attention to the land, that thou mayest have lambs.
verses.27: My son, thou hast from me words very useful for thy life, and for the life of thy servants.

verses.1: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.2: Son of man, speak to the children of thy people, and thou shalt say to them, On whatsoever land I shall bring a sword, and the people of the land take one man of them, and set him for their watchman:
verses.3: and he shall see the sword coming upon the land, and blow the trumpet, and sound an alarm to the people;
verses.4: and he that hears the sound of the trumpet shall hear indeed, and yet not take heed, and the sword shall come upon him, and overtake him, his blood shall be upon his own head.
verses.5: Because he heard the sound of the trumpet, and took no heed, his blood shall be upon him: but the other, because he took heed, has delivered his soul.
verses.6: But if the watchman see the sword coming, and do not sound the trumpet, and the people do not watch; and the sword come, and take a soul from among them, that soul is taken because of its iniquity; but the blood thereof will I require at the watchman's hand.
verses.7: And thou, son of man, I have set thee as a watchman to the house of Israel, and thou shalt hear a word from my mouth.
verses.8: When I say to the sinner, Thou shalt surely die; if thou speak not to warn the wicked from his way, the wicked himself shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.
verses.9: But if thou forewarn the wicked of his way to turn from it, and he turn not from his way, he shall die in his ungodliness; but thou hast delivered thine own soul.
verses.10: And thou, son of man, say to the house of Israel; Thus have ye spoken, saying, Our errors, and our iniquities weigh upon us, and we pine away in them, and how then shall we live?
verses.11: Say to them, Thus saith the Lord; As I live, I desire not the death of the ungodly, as that the ungodly should turn from his way and live: turn ye heartily from your way; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
verses.12: Say to the children of thy people, The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him, in the day wherein he errs: and the iniquity of the ungodly shall not harm him, in the day wherein he turns from his iniquity, but the righteous erring shall not be able to deliver himself.
verses.13: When I say to the righteous, Thou shalt live; and he trusts in his righteousness, and shall commit iniquity, none of his righteousnesses shall be remembered; in his unrighteousness which he has wrought, in it shall he die.
verses.14: And when I say to the ungodly, Thou shalt surely die; and he shall turn from his sin, and do judgment and justice,
verses.15: and return the pledge, and repay that which he has robbed, and walk in the ordinances of life, so as to do no wrong; he shall surely live, and shall not die.
verses.16: None of his sins which he has committed shall be remembered: because he has wrought judgment and righteousness; by them shall he live.
verses.17: Yet the children of thy people will say, The way of the Lord is not straight: whereas this their way is not straight.
verses.18: When the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and shall commit iniquities, then shall he die in them.
verses.19: And when the sinner turns from his iniquity, and shall do judgment and righteousness, he shall live by them.
verses.20: And this is that which ye said, The way of the Lord is not straight. I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one for his ways.
verses.21: And it came to pass in the tenth year of our captivity, in the twelfth month, on the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped from Jerusalem came to me, saying, The city is taken.
verses.22: Now the hand of the Lord had come upon me in the evening, before he came; and he opened my mouth, when he came to me in the morning: and my mouth was open, it was no longer kept closed.
verses.23: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.24: Son of man, they that inhabit the desolate places on the land of Israel say, Abraam was one, and he possessed the land: and we are more numerous; to us the land is given for a possession.
verses.25: Therefore say to them, Thus saith the Lord God,
verses.27: As I live, surely they that are in the desolate places shall fall by swords, and they that are in the open plain shall be given for food to the wild beasts of the field, and them that are in the fortified cities and them that are in the caves I will slay with pestilence.
verses.28: And I will make the land desert, and the pride of her strength shall perish; and the mountains of Israel shall be made desolate by reason of no man passing through.
verses.29: And they shall know that I am the Lord; and I will make their land desert, and it shall be made desolate because of all their abominations which they have wrought.
verses.30: And as for thee, son of man, the children of thy people are they that speak concerning thee by the walls, and in the porches of the houses, and they talk one to another, saying, Let us come together, and let us hear the words that proceed from the Lord.
verses.31: They approach thee as a people comes together, and sit before thee, and hear thy words, but they will not do them: for there is falsehood in their mouth, and their heart goes after their pollutions.
verses.32: And thou art to them as the sound of a sweet, well-tuned psaltery, and they will hear thy words, but they will not do them.
verses.33: But whenever it shall come to pass, they will say, Behold, it is come: and they shall know that there was a prophet in the midst of them.

verses.1: And Roboam came to Jerusalem; and he assembled Juda and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand young men fit for war, and he waged war with Israel to recover the kingdom to Roboam.
verses.2: And the word of the Lord came to Samaias the man of God, saying,
verses.3: Speak to Roboam the son of Solomon, and to all Juda and Benjamin, saying,
verses.4: Thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not go up, and ye shall not war against your brethren: return every one to his home; for this thing is of me. And they hearkened to the word of the Lord, and returned from going against Jeroboam.
verses.5: And Roboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and he built walled cities in Judæa.
verses.6: And he built Bethleem, and Ætan and Thecoe,
verses.7: and Bæthsura, and Sochoth, and Odollam,
verses.8: and Geth, and Marisa, and Ziph,
verses.9: and Adorai, and Lachis, and Azeca,
verses.10: and Saraa, and Ælom, and Chebron, which belongs to Juda and Benjamin, walled cities.
verses.11: And he fortified them with walls, and placed in them captains, and stores of provisions, oil and wine,
verses.12: shields and spears in every several city, and he fortified them very strongly, and he had on his side Juda and Benjamin.
verses.13: And the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel were gathered to him out of all the coasts.
verses.14: For the Levites left the tents of their possession, and went to Juda to Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had ejected them so that they should not minister to the Lord.
verses.15: And he made for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vanities, and for the calves which Jeroboam made.
verses.16: And he cast out from the tribes of Israel those who set their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel: and they came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.17: And they strengthened the kingdom of Juda; and Juda strengthened Roboam the son of Solomon for three years, for he walked three years in the ways of David and Solomon.
verses.18: And Roboam took to himself for a wife Moolath daughter of Jerimuth the son of David, and Abigaia daughter of Heliab the son of Jessæ.
verses.19: And she bore him sons; Jeus, and Samoria, and Zaam.
