verses.20: And afterwards he took to himself Maacha the daughter of Abessalom; and she bore him Abia, and Jetthi, and Zeza, and Salemoth.
verses.21: And Roboam loved Maacha the daughter of Abessalom more than all his wives and all his concubines: for he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines; and he begot twenty-eight sons, and sixty daughters.
verses.22: And he made Abia the son of Maacha chief, even a leader among his brethren, for he intended to make him king.
verses.23: And he was exalted beyond all his other sons in all the coasts of Juda and Benjamin, and in the strong cities; and he gave them provisions in great abundance: and he desired many wives.

verses.1: And it came to pass when king Ezekias heard it, that he rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
verses.2: And he sent Heliakim the steward, and Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, clothed with sackcloth, to Esaias the prophet the son of Amos.
verses.3: And they said to him, Thus says Ezekias, This day is a day of tribulation, and rebuke, and provocation: for the children are come to the travail-pangs, but the mother has no strength.
verses.4: Peradventure the Lord thy God will hear all the words of Rapsakes, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to reproach the living God and to revile him with the words which the Lord thy God has heard: and thou shalt offer thy prayer for the remnant that is found.
verses.5: So the servants of king Ezekias came to Esaias.
verses.6: And Esaias said to them, Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith the Lord, Be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed.
verses.7: Behold, I send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a report, and shall return to his own land; and I will overthrow him with the sword in his own land.
verses.8: So Rapsakes returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Lobna: for he heard that he had departed from Lachis.
verses.9: And he heard concerning Tharaca king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he is come forth to fight with thee: and he returned, and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying,
verses.10: Let not thy God on whom thou trustest encourage thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be delivered into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.
verses.11: Behold, thou hast heard all that the kings of the Assyrians have done in all the lands, to waste them utterly: and shalt thou be delivered?
verses.12: Have the gods of the nations at all delivered them, whom my fathers destroyed; both Gozan, and Charran, and Raphis, and the sons of Edem who were in Thaesthen?
verses.13: Where is the king of Hæmath, and the king of Arphad? and where is the king of the city of Seppharvaim, of Ana, and Aba?
verses.14: And Ezekias took the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it: and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Ezekias spread it before the Lord,
verses.15: and said, O Lord God of Israel, that dwellest over the cherubs, thou art the only God in all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.
verses.16: Incline thine ear, O Lord, and hear: open, Lord, thine eyes, and see: and hear the words of Sennacherim, which he has sent to reproach the living God.
verses.17: For truly, Lord, the kings of Assyria have wasted the nations,
verses.18: and have cast their gods into the fire: because they are no gods, but the works of men's hands, wood and stone; and they have destroyed them.
verses.19: And now, O Lord our God, deliver us out of his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth shall know that thou alone art the Lord God.
verses.20: And Esaias the son of Amos sent to Ezekias, saying, Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, I have heard thy prayer to me concerning Sennacherim king of the Assyrians.
verses.21: This is the word which the Lord has spoken against him; The virgin daughter of Sion has made light of thee, and mocked thee; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at thee.
verses.22: Whom hast thou reproached, and whom hast thou reviled? and against whom hast thou lifted up thy voice, and raised thine eyes on high? Is it against the Holy One of Israel?
verses.23: By thy messengers thou hast reproached the Lord, and hast said, I will go up with the multitude of my chariots, to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Libanus, and I have cut down the height of his cedar, and his choice cypresses; and I have come into the midst of the forest and of Carmel.
verses.24: I have refreshed myself, and have drunk strange waters, and I have dried up with the sole of my foot all the rivers of fortified places.
verses.25: I have brought about the matter, I have brought it to a conclusion; and it is come to the destruction of the bands of warlike prisoners, even of strong cities.
verses.26: And they that dwelt in them were weak in hand, they quaked and were confounded, they became as grass of the field, or as the green herb, the grass growing on houses, and that which is trodden down by him that stands upon it.
verses.27: But I know thy down-sitting, and thy going forth, and thy rage against me.
verses.28: Because thou wast angry against me, and thy fierceness is come up into my ears, therefore will I put my hooks in thy nostrils, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.
verses.29: And this shall be a sign to thee; eat this year the things that grow of themselves, and in the second year the things which spring up: and in the third year let there be sowing, and reaping, and planting of vineyards, and eat ye the fruit of them.
verses.30: And he shall increase him that has escaped of the house of Juda: and the remnant shall strike root beneath, and it shall produce fruit above.
verses.31: For from Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and he that escapes from the mountain of Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.
verses.32: Is it not so? Thus saith the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians, He shall not enter into this city, and he shall not shoot an arrow there, neither shall a shield come against it, neither shall he heap a mound against it.
verses.33: By the way by which he comes, by it shall he return, and he shall not enter into this city, saith the Lord.
verses.34: And I will defend this city as with a shield, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake.
verses.35: And it came to pass at night that the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand: and they rose early in the morning, and, behold, these were all dead corpses.
verses.36: And Sennacherim king of the Assyrians departed, and went and returned, and dwelt in Nineve.
verses.37: And it came to pass, while he was worshipping in the house of Meserach his god, that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Ararath; and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.

verses.1: And Elisaie said, Hear thou the word of the Lord; Thus saith the Lord, As at this time, to-morrow a measure of fine flour shall be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gates of Samaria.
verses.2: And the officer on whose hand the king rested, answered Elisaie, and said, Behold, if the Lord shall make flood-gates in heaven, might this thing be? and Elisaie said, Behold, thou shalt see with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.
verses.3: And there were four leprous men by the gate of the city: and one said to his neighbour, Why sit we here until we die?
verses.4: If we should say, Let us go into the city, then there is famine in the city, and we shall die there: and if we sit here, then we shall die. Now then come, and let us fall upon the camp of the Syrians: if they should take us alive, then we shall live; and if they should put us to death, then we shall only die.
verses.5: And they rose up while it was yet night, to go into the camp of Syria; and they came into a part of the camp of Syria, and behold, there was no man there.
verses.6: For the Lord had made the army of Syria to hear a sound of chariots, and a sound of horses, even the sound of a great host: and each man said to his fellow, Now has the king of Israel hired against us the kings of the Chettites, and the kings of Egypt, to come against us.
verses.7: And they arose and fled while it was yet dark, and left their tents, and their horses, and their asses in the camp, as they were, and fled for their lives.
verses.8: And these lepers entered a little way into the camp, and went into one tent, and ate and drank, and took thence silver, and gold, and raiment; and they went and returned thence, and entered into another tent, and took thence, and went and hid the spoil.
verses.9: And one man said to his neighbour, We are not doing well thus: this day is a day of glad tidings, and we hold our peace, and are waiting till the morning light, and shall find mischief: now then come, and let us go into the city, and report to the house of the king.
verses.10: So they went and cried toward the gate of the city, and reported to them, saying, We went into the camp of Syria, and, behold, there is not there a man, nor voice of man, only horses tied and asses, and their tents as they were.
verses.11: And the porters cried aloud, and reported to the house of the king within.
verses.12: And the king rose up by night, and said to his servants, I will now tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They knew that we are hungry; and they have gone forth from the camp and hidden themselves in the field, saying, They will come out of the city, and we shall catch them alive, and go into the city.
verses.13: And one of his servants answered and said, Let them now take five of the horses that were left, which were left here; behold, they are the number left to all the multitude of Israel; and we will send thither and see.
verses.14: So they took two horsemen; and the king of Israel sent after the king of Syria, saying, Go, and see.
verses.15: And they went after them even to Jordan: and, behold, all the way was full of garments and vessels, which the Syrians had cast away in their panic. And the messengers returned, and brought word to the king.
verses.16: And the people went out, and plundered the camp of Syria: and a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, according to the word of the Lord, and two measures of barley for a shekel.
verses.17: And the king appointed the officer on whose hand the king leaned to have charge over the gate: and the people trampled on him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had said, who spoke when the messenger came down to him.
verses.18: So it came to pass as Elisaie had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley shall be sold for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel; and it shall be as at this time to-morrow in the gate of Samaria.
verses.19: And the officer answered Elisaie, and said, Behold, if the Lord makes flood-gates in heaven, shall this thing be? and Elisaie said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not eat thereof.
verses.20: And it was so: for the people trampled on him in the gate, and he died.

verses.1: And he brought me into the inner court eastward, opposite the northern gate: and he brought me in, and behold five chambers near the vacant space, and near the northern partition,
verses.2: a hundred cubits in length toward the north, and in breadth fifty,
verses.3: ornamented accordingly as the gates of the inner court, and arranged accordingly as the peristyles of the outer court, with triple porticos fronting one another.
verses.4: And in front of the chambers was a walk ten cubits in breadth, the length reaching to a hundred cubits; and their doors were northward.
verses.5: And the upper walks were in like manner: for the peristyle projected from it, even from the range of columns below, and there was a space between; so were there a peristyle and a space between, and so were there two porticos.
verses.6: For they were triple, and they had not pillars like the pillars of the outer ones: therefore they projected from the lower ones and the middle ones from the ground.
verses.7: And there was light without, corresponding to the chambers of the outer court looking toward the front of the northern chambers; the length of them was fifty cubits.
verses.8: For the length of the chambers looking toward the inner court was fifty cubits, and these are the ones that front the others; the whole was a hundred cubits.
verses.9: And there were doors of these chambers for an outlet towards the east, so that one should go through them out of the outer court,
verses.10: by the opening of the walk at the corner; and the south parts were toward the south, toward the remaining space, and toward the partition, and so were the chambers.
verses.11: And the walk was in front of them, according to the measures of the chambers toward the north, both according to the length of them, and according to the breadth of them, and according to all their openings, and according to all their turnings, and according to their lights, and according to their doors.
verses.12: So were the measures of the chambers toward the south, and according to the doors at the entrance of the walk, as it were the distance of a reed for light, and eastward as one went in by them.
verses.13: And he said to me, The chambers toward the north, and the chambers toward the south, in front of the void spaces, these are the chambers of the sanctuary, wherein the priests the sons of Sadduc, who draw nigh to the Lord, shall eat the most holy things: and there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meat-offering, and the sin-offerings, and the trespass-offerings; because the place is holy.
verses.14: None shall go in thither except the priests, and they shall not go forth of the holy place into the outer court, that they that draw nigh to me may be continually holy, and may not touch their garments in which they minister, with defilement, for they are holy; and they shall put on other garments whenever they come in contact with the people.
verses.15: So the measurement of the house within was accomplished: and he brought me forth by the way of the gate that looks eastward, and measured the plan of the house round about in order.
verses.16: And he stood behind the gate looking eastward, and measured five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
verses.17: And he turned to the north and measured in front of the north side five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
verses.18: And he turned to the west, and measured in front of the west side, five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
verses.19: And he turned to the south, and measured in front of the south side, five hundred cubits by the measuring reed.
verses.20: The four sides he measured by the same reed, and he marked out the house and the circumference of the parts round about, a space of five hundred cubits eastward, and a breadth of five hundred cubits, to make a division between the sanctuary and the outer wall, that belonged to the design of the house.

verses.1: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.2: And thou, son of man, wilt thou judge the bloody city? yea, declare thou to her all her iniquities.
verses.3: And thou shalt say, Thus saith the Lord God: O city that sheds blood in the midst of her, so that her time should come, and that forms devices against herself, to defile herself;
verses.4: in their blood which thou hast shed, thou hast transgressed; and in thy devices which thou hast formed, thou hast polluted thyself; and thou hast brought nigh thy days, and hast brought on the time of thy years: therefore have I made thee a reproach to the Gentiles, and a mockery to all the countries,
verses.5: to those near thee, and to those far distant from thee; and they shall mock thee, thou that art notoriously unclean, and abundant in iniquities.
verses.6: Behold, the princes of the house of Israel have conspired in thee each one with his kindred, that they might shed blood.
verses.7: In thee they have reviled father and mother; and in thee they have behaved unjustly toward the stranger: they have oppressed the orphan and widow.
verses.8: And they have set at nought my holy things, and in thee they have profaned my sabbaths.
verses.9: There are robbers in thee, to shed blood in thee; and in thee they have eaten upon the mountains: they have wrought ungodliness in the midst of thee.
verses.10: In thee they have uncovered the father's shame; and in thee they have humbled her that was set apart for uncleanness.
verses.11: They have dealt unlawfully each one with his neighbour's wife; and each one in ungodliness has defiled his daughter-in-law: and in thee they have humbled each one his sister, the daughter of his father.
verses.12: In thee they have received gifts to shed blood; they have received in thee interest and usurious increase; and by oppression thou hast brought thy wickedness to the full, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord.
verses.13: And if I shall smite my hand at thine iniquities which thou hast accomplished, which thou hast wrought, and at thy blood that has been shed in the midst of thee,
verses.14: shall thy heart endure? shall thine hands be strong in the days which I bring upon thee? I the Lord have spoken, and will do it.
verses.15: And I will scatter thee among the nations, and disperse thee in the countries, and thy uncleanness shall be removed out of thee.
verses.16: And I will give heritages in thee in the sight of the nations, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.17: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.18: Son of man, behold, the house of Israel are all become to me as it were mixed with brass, and iron, and tin, and lead; they are mixed up in the midst of silver.
verses.19: Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; Because ye have become one mixture, therefore I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.
verses.20: As silver, and brass, and iron, and tin, and lead, are gathered into the midst of the furnace, to blow fire into it, that they may be melted: so will I take you in my wrath, and I will gather and melt you.
verses.21: And I will blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof.
verses.22: As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so shall ye be melted in the midst thereof; and ye shall know that I the Lord have poured out my wrath upon you.
verses.23: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.24: Son of man, say to her, Thou art the land that is not rained upon, neither has rain come upon thee in the day of wrath:
verses.25: whose princes in the midst of her are as roaring lions seizing prey, devouring souls by oppression, and taking bribes; and thy widows are multiplied in the midst of thee.
verses.26: Her priests also have set at nought my law, and profaned my holy things: they have not distinguished between the holy and profane, nor have they distinguished between the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I was profaned in the midst of them.
verses.27: Her princes in the midst of her are as wolves ravening to shed blood, that they may get dishonest gain.
verses.28: And her prophets that daub them shall fall, that see vanities, that prophesy falsehoods, saying, Thus saith the Lord, when the Lord has not spoken.
verses.29: That sorely oppress the people of the land with injustice, and commit robbery; oppressing the poor and needy, and not dealing justly with the stranger.
verses.30: And I sought from among them a man behaving uprightly, and standing before me perfectly in the time of wrath, so that I should not utterly destroy her: but I found him not.
verses.31: So I have poured out my wrath upon her in the fury of mine anger, to accomplish it. I have recompensed their ways on their own heads, saith the Lord God.

verses.1: Then came all the leaders of the host, and Joanan, and Azarias the son of Maasæas, and all the people great and small,
verses.2: to Jeremias the prophet, and said to him, Let now our supplication come before thy face, and pray thou to the Lord thy God for this remnant; for we are left few out of many, as thine eyes see.
verses.3: And let the Lord thy God declare to us the way wherein we should walk, and the thing which we should do.
verses.4: And Jeremias said to them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray for you to the Lord our God, according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever word the Lord God shall answer, I will declare it to you; I will not hide anything from you.
verses.5: And they said to Jeremias, Let the Lord be between us for a just and faithful witness, if we do not according to every word which the Lord shall send to us.
verses.6: And whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will hearken to the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, because we shall hearken to the voice of the Lord our God.
verses.7: And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the Lord came to Jeremias.
verses.8: And he called Joanan, and the leaders of the host, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.9: and he said to them, Thus saith the Lord;
verses.10: If ye will indeed dwell in this land, I will build you, and will not pull you down, but will plant you, and in no wise pluck you up: for I have ceased from the calamities which I brought upon you.
verses.11: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid; be not afraid of him, saith the Lord: for I am with you, to deliver you, and save you out of their hand.
verses.12: And I will grant you mercy, and pity you, and will restore you to your land.
verses.13: But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, that we may not hearken to the voice of the Lord;
verses.14: for we will go into the land of Egypt, and we shall see no war, and shall not hear the sound of a trumpet, and we shall not hunger for bread; and there we will dwell:
verses.15: then hear the word of the Lord; thus saith the Lord;
verses.16: If ye set your face toward Egypt, and go in there to dwell; then it shall be, that the sword which ye fear shall find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine to which ye have regard, shall overtake you, coming after you in Egypt; and there ye shall die.
verses.17: And all the men, and all the strangers who have set their face toward the land of Egypt to dwell there, shall be consumed by the sword, and by the famine: and there shall not one of them escape from the evils which I bring upon them.
verses.18: For thus saith the Lord; As my wrath has dropped upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so shall my wrath drop upon you, when ye have entered into Egypt: and ye shall be a desolation, and under the power of others, and a curse and a reproach: and ye shall no more see this place.
verses.19: These are the words which the Lord has spoken concerning you the remnant of Juda; Enter ye not into Egypt: and now know ye for a certainty,
verses.20: that ye have wrought wickedness in your hearts, when ye sent me, saying, Pray thou for us to the Lord; and according to all that the Lord shall speak to thee we will do.
verses.21: And ye have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord, with which he sent me to you.
verses.22: Now therefore ye shall perish by sword and by famine, in the place which ye desire to go into to dwell there.

verses.1: And one of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried to Elisaie, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant feared the Lord: and the creditor is come to take my two sons to be his servants.
verses.2: And Elisaie said, What shall I do for thee? tell me what thou hast in the house. And she said, Thy servant has nothing in the house, except oil wherewith I anoint myself.
verses.3: And he said to her, Go, borrow for thyself vessels without of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.
verses.4: And thou shalt go in and shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and thou shalt pour forth into these vessels, and remove that which is filled.
verses.5: And she departed from him, and shut the door upon herself and upon her sons: they brought the vessels near to her, and she poured in until the vessels were filled.
verses.6: And she said to her sons, Bring me yet a vessel. And they said to her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
verses.7: And she came and told the man of God: and Elisaie said, Go, and sell the oil, and thou shalt pay thy debts, and thou and thy sons shall live of the remaining oil.
verses.8: And a day came, when Elisaie passed over to Soman, and there was a great lady there, and she constrained him to eat bread: and it came to pass as often as he went into the city, that he turned aside to eat there.
verses.9: And the woman said to her husband, See now, I know that this is a holy man of God who comes over continually to us.
verses.10: Let us now make for him an upper chamber, a small place; and let us put there for him a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall come to pass that when he comes in to us, he shall turn in thither.
verses.11: And a day came, and he went in thither, and turned aside into the upper chamber, and lay there.
verses.12: And he said to Giezi his servant, Call me this Somanite. And he called her, and she stood before him.
verses.13: And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, thou hast taken all this trouble for us; what should I do for thee? Hast thou any request to make to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she said, I dwell in the midst of my people.
verses.14: And he said to Giezi, What must we do for her? and Giezi his servant said, Indeed she has no son, and her husband is old.
verses.15: And he called her, and she stood by the door.
verses.16: And Elisaie said to her, At this time next year, as the season is, thou shalt be alive, and embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, do not lie to thy servant.
verses.17: And the woman conceived, and bore a son at the very time, as the season was, being alive, as Elisaie said to her.
verses.18: And the child grew: and it came to pass when he went out to his father to the reapers,
verses.19: that he said to his father, My head, my head. And his father said to a servant, Carry him to his mother.
verses.20: And he carried him to his mother, and he lay upon her knees till noon, and died.
verses.21: And she carried him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God; and she shut the door upon him, and went out.
verses.22: And she called her husband, and said, Send now for me one of the young men, and one of the asses, and I will ride quickly to the man of God, and return.
verses.23: And he said, Why art thou going to him to-day? It is neither new moon, nor the sabbath. And she said, It is well.
verses.24: And she saddled the ass, and said to her servant, Be quick, proceed: spare not on my account to ride, unless I shall tell thee. Go, and thou shalt proceed, and come to the man of God to mount Carmel.
verses.25: And she rode and came to the man of God to the mountain: and it came to pass when Elisaie saw her coming, that he said to Giezi his servant, See now, that Somanite comes.
verses.26: Now run to meet her, and thou shalt say, Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? and she said, It is well.
verses.27: And she came to Elisaie to the mountain, and laid hold of his feet; and Giezi drew near to thrust her away. And Elisaie said, Let her alone, for her soul is much grieved in her, and the Lord has hidden it from me, and has not told it me.
verses.28: And she said, Did I ask a son of my lord? For did I not say, Do not deal deceitfully with me?
verses.29: And Elisaie said to Giezi, Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thy hand, and go: if thou meet any man, thou shalt not salute him, and if a man salute thee thou shalt not answer him: and thou shalt lay my staff on the child's face.
verses.30: And the mother of the child said, As the Lord lives and as thy soul lives, I will not leave thee. And Elisaie arose, and went after her.
verses.31: And Giezi went on before her, and laid his staff on the child's face: but there was neither voice nor any hearing. So he returned to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not awaked.
verses.32: And Elisaie went into the house, and, behold, the dead child was laid upon his bed.
verses.33: And Elisaie went into the house, and shut the door upon themselves, the two, and prayed to the Lord.
verses.34: And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and bowed himself upon him, and the flesh of the child grew warm.
verses.35: And he returned, and walked up and down in the house: and he went up, and bowed himself on the child seven times; and the child opened his eyes.
verses.36: And Elisaie cried out to Giezi, and said, Call this Somanite. So he called her, and she came in to him: and Elisaie said, Take thy son.
verses.37: And the woman went in, and fell at his feet, and did obeisance bowing to the ground; and she took her son, and went out.
verses.38: And Elisaie returned to Galgala: and a famine was in the land; and the sons of the prophets sat before him: and Elisaie said to his servant, Set on the great pot, and boil pottage for the sons of the prophets.
verses.39: And he went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a vine in the field, and gathered of it wild gourds, his garment full; and he cast it into the caldron of pottage, for they knew them not.
verses.40: And he poured it out for the men to eat: and it came to pass, when they were eating of the pottage, that lo! they cried out, and said, There is death in the pot, O man of God. And they could not eat.
verses.41: And he said, Take meal, and cast it into the pot. And Elisaie said to his servant Giezi, Pour out for the people, and let them eat. And there was no longer there any hurtful thing in the pot.
verses.42: And there came a man over from Bætharisa, and brought to the man of God twenty barley loaves and cakes of figs, of the first-fruits. And he said, Give to the people, and let them eat.
verses.43: And his servant said, Why should I set this before a hundred men? and he said, Give to the people, and let them eat; for thus saith the Lord, They shall eat and leave.
verses.44: And they ate and left, according to the word of the Lord.

verses.1: And David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel in his stead.
verses.2: And he assembled all the chief men of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites.
verses.3: And the Levites numbered themselves from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls amounted to thirty and eight thousand men.
verses.4: Of the overseers over the works of the house of the Lord there were twenty-four thousand, and there were six thousand scribes and judges;
verses.5: and four thousand door-keepers, and four thousand to praise the Lord with instruments which he made to praise the Lord.
verses.6: And David divided them into daily courses, for the sons of Levi, for Gedson, Caath, and Merari.
verses.7: And for the family of Gedson, Edan, and Semei.
verses.8: The sons of Edan were Jeiel, the chief, and Zethan, and Joel, three.
verses.9: The sons of Semei; Salomith, Jeiel, and Dan, three: these were the chiefs of the families of Edan.
verses.10: And to the sons of Semei, Jeth, and Ziza, and Joas, and Beria: these were the four sons of Semei.
verses.11: And Jeth was the chief, and Ziza the second: and Joas and Beria did not multiply sons, and they became only one reckoning according to the house of their father.
verses.12: The sons of Caath; Ambram, Isaar, Chebron, Oziel, four.
verses.13: The sons of Ambram; Aaron and Moses: and Aaron was appointed for the consecration of the most holy things, he and his sons for ever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister and bless in his name for ever.
verses.14: And as for Moses the man of God, his sons were reckoned to the tribe of Levi.
verses.15: The sons of Moses; Gersam, and Eliezer.
verses.16: The sons of Gersam; Subael the chief.
verses.17: And the sons of Eliezer were, Rabia the chief: and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rabia were very greatly multiplied.
verses.18: The sons of Isaar; Salomoth the chief.
verses.19: The sons of Chebron; Jeria the chief, Amaria the second, Jeziel the third, Jekemias the fourth.
verses.20: The sons of Oziel; Micha the chief, and Isia the second.
verses.21: The sons of Merari; Mooli, and Musi: the sons of Mooli; Eleazar, and Kis.
verses.22: And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, but daughters: and the sons of Kis, their brethren, took them.
verses.23: The sons of Musi; Mooli, and Eder, and Jarimoth, three.
verses.24: These are the sons of Levi according to the houses of their fathers; chiefs of their families according to their numbering, according to the number of their names, according to their polls, doing the works of service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward.
verses.25: For David said, The Lord God of Israel has given rest to his people, and has taken up his abode in Jerusalem for ever.
verses.26: And the Levites bore not the tabernacle, and all the vessels of it for its service.
verses.27: For by the last words of David was the number of the Levites taken from twenty years old and upward.
verses.28: For he appointed them to wait on Aaron, to minister in the house of the Lord, over the courts, and over the chambers, and over the purification of all the holy things, and over the works of the service of the house of God;
verses.29: and for the shew-bread, and for the fine flour of the meat-offering, and for the unleavened cakes, and for the fried cake, and for the dough, and for every measure;
verses.30: and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks to the Lord, and so in the evening;
verses.31: and to be over all the whole-burnt-offerings that were offered up to the Lord on the sabbaths, and at the new moons, and at the feasts, by number, according to the order given to them, continually before the Lord.
verses.32: And they are to keep the charge of the tabernacle of witness, and the charge of the holy place, and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brethren, to minister in the house of the Lord.

verses.1: And in the eighth year Jodae strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azarias the son of Joram, and Ismael the son of Joanan, and Azarias the son of Obed, and Maasæas the son of Adia, and Elisaphan the son of Zacharias, with him into the house of the Lord.
verses.2: And they went round about Juda, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Juda, and heads of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.3: And all the congregation of Juda made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he shewed them the king's son, and said to them, Lo, let the king's son reign, as the Lord said concerning the house of David.
verses.4: Now this is the thing which ye shall do. Let a third part of you, even of the priests and of the Levites, enter in on the sabbath, even into the gates of the entrances;
verses.5: and let a third part be in the house of the king; and another third at the middle gate: and all the people in the courts of the Lord's house.
verses.6: And let not any one enter into the house of the Lord, except the priests and the Levites, and the servants of the Levites; they shall enter in, because they are holy: and let all the people keep the watch of the Lord.
verses.7: And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man's weapon in his hand; and whoever else goes into the house shall die: but they shall be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in.
verses.8: And the Levites and all Juda did according to all that the priest Jodae commanded them, and they took each his men from the beginning of the sabbath to the end of the sabbath, for Jodae the priest did not dismiss the courses.
verses.9: And Jodae gave to the men the swords, and the shields, and the arms, which had belonged to king David, in the house of God.
verses.10: And he set the whole people, every man with his arms, from the right side of the house to the left side of the altar and the house, over against the king round about.
verses.11: And he brought out the king's son, and put on him the crown and the testimony, and Jodae the priest and his sons proclaimed him king, and anointed him, and said, Long live the king!
verses.12: And Gotholia heard the sound of the people running, and acknowledging and praising the king: and she went in to the king into the house of the Lord.
verses.13: And she looked, and, behold, the king stood in his place, and the princes and trumpets were at the entrance, and the princes were round the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded the trumpets, and there were the singers singing with instruments, and singing hymns of praise. And Gotholia rent her robe, and cried, Ye surely are plotting against me.
verses.14: And Jodae the priest went forth, and Jodae the priest charged the captains of hundreds, even the captains of the host, and said to them, Thrust her forth outside the house, and follow her, and let her be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.
verses.15: So they let her go out; and she went through the horsemen's gate of the house of the king, and they slew her there.
verses.16: And Jodae made a covenant between himself, and the people, and the king, that the people should be the Lord's.
verses.17: And all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and tore down it and its altars, and they ground his images to powder, and they slew Matthan the priest of Baal before his altars.
verses.18: And Jodae the priest committed the works of the house of the Lord into the hand of the priests and Levites, and he re-established the courses of the priests and Levites which David appointed over the house of the Lord, and he appointed them to offer whole-burnt-offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with gladness, and with songs by the hand of David.
verses.19: And the porters stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, that no one unclean in any respect should enter in.
verses.20: And he took the heads of families, and the mighty men, and the chiefs of the people, and all the people of the land, and they conducted the king into the house of the Lord; and he went through the inner gate into the king's house, and they seated the king on the throne of the kingdom.
verses.21: And all the people of the land rejoiced; and the city was quiet: and they slew Gotholia.

verses.1: And I lifted up mine eyes and looked, and behold four horns.
verses.2: And I said to the angel that spoke with me, What are these things, my lord? And he said to me, These are the horns that have scattered Juda, and Israel, and Jerusalem.
verses.3: And the Lord shewed me four artificers.
verses.4: And I said, What are these coming to do? And he said, These are the horns that scattered Juda, and they broke Israel in pieces, and none of them lifted up his head: and these are come forth to sharpen them for their hands, even the four horns, the nations that lifted up the horn against the land of the Lord to scatter it.
verses.5: And I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a man, and in his hand a measuring line.
verses.6: And I said to him, Whither goest thou? And he said to me, To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth of it, and what is the length of it.
verses.7: And, behold, the angel that spoke with me stood by, and another angel went forth to meet him,
verses.8: and spoke to him, saying, Run and speak to that young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be fully inhabited by reason of the abundance of men and cattle in the midst of her.
verses.9: And I will be to her, saith the Lord, a wall of fire round about, and I will be for a glory in the midst of her.
verses.10: Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I will gather you from the four winds of heaven, saith the Lord,
verses.11: even to Sion: deliver yourselves, ye that dwell with the daughter of Babylon.
verses.12: For thus saith the Lord Almighty; After the glory has he sent me to the nations that spoiled you: for he that touches you is as one that touches the apple of his eye.
verses.13: For, behold, I bring my hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to them that serve them: and ye shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.
verses.14: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Sion: for, behold, I come, and will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the Lord.
verses.15: And many nations shall flee for refuge to the Lord in that day, and they shall be for a people to him, and they shall dwell in the midst of thee: and thou shalt know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to thee.
verses.16: And the Lord shall inherit Juda his portion in the holy land, and he will yet choose Jerusalem.
verses.17: Let all flesh fear before the Lord: for he has risen up from his holy clouds.

verses.1: And this is all Israel, even their enrolment: and these are written down in the book of the kings of Israel and Juda, with the names of them that were carried away to Babylon for their transgressions.
verses.2: And they that dwelt before in their possessions in the cities of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the appointed ones.
verses.3: And there dwelt in Jerusalem some of the children of Juda, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasse.
verses.4: And Gnothi, and the son of Samiud, the son of Amri, the son of Ambraim, the son of Buni, son of the sons of Phares, the son of Juda.
verses.5: And of the Selonites; Asaia his first-born, and his sons.
verses.6: Of the sons of Zara; Jeel, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety.
verses.7: And of the sons of Benjamin; Salom, son of Mosollam, son of Odouia, son of Asinu.
verses.8: And Jemnaa son of Jeroboam, and Elo: these are the sons of Ozi the son of Machir: and Mosollam, son of Saphatia, son of Raguel, son of Jemnai;
verses.9: and their brethren according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty-six, all the men were heads of families according to the houses of their fathers.
verses.10: And of the priests; Jodaë, and Joarim, and Jachin,
verses.11: and Azaria the son of Chelcias, the son of Mosollam, the son of Sadoc, the son of Maraïoth, the son of Achitob, the ruler of the house of God;
verses.12: and Adaia son of Iraam, son of Phascor, son of Melchia, and Maasaia son of Adiel, son of Ezira, son of Mosollam, son of Maselmoth, son of Emmer;
verses.13: and their brethren, chiefs of their families, a thousand seven hundred and sixty, mighty men for the work of the ministration of the house of God.
verses.14: And of the Levites; Samaia son of Asob, son of Ezricam, son of Asabia, of the sons of Merari.
verses.15: And Bacbacar, and Ares, and Galaal, and Matthanias son of Micha, son of Zechri, son of Asaph;
verses.16: and Abdia, son of Samia, son of Galaal, son of Idithun, and Barachia son of Ossa, son of Helcana—who dwelt in the villages of the Notephatites.
verses.17: The door-keepers; Salom, Acum, Telmon, and Diman, and their brethren; Salom was the chief;
verses.18: and he waited hitherto in the king's gate eastward: these are the gates of the companies of the sons of Levi.
verses.19: And Sellum the son of Core, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Core, and his brethren belonging to the house of his father, the Corites were over the works of the service, keeping the watches of the tabernacle, and their fathers over the camp of the Lord, keeping the entrance.
verses.20: And Phinees son of Eleazar was head over them before the Lord, and these were with him.
verses.21: Zacharias the son of Mosollami was keeper of the door of the tabernacle of witness.
verses.22: All the chosen porters in the gates were two hundred and twelve, these were in their courts, this was their distribution: these David and Samuel the seer established in their charge.
verses.23: And these and their sons were over the gates in the house of the Lord, and in the house of the tabernacle, to keep watch.
verses.24: The gates were toward the four winds, eastward, westward, northward, southward.
verses.25: And their brethren were in their courts, to enter in weekly from time to time with these.
verses.26: For four strong men have the charge of the gates; and the Levites were over the chambers, and they keep watch over the treasures of the house of God.
verses.27: For the charge was upon them, and these were charged with the keys to open the doors of the temple every morning.
verses.28: And some of them were appointed over the vessels of service, that they should carry them in by number, and carry them out by number.
verses.29: And some of them were appointed over the furniture, and over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
verses.30: And some of the priests were makers of the ointment, and appointed to prepare the spices.
verses.31: And Matthathias of the Levites, (he was the first-born of Salom the Corite,) was set in charge over the sacrifices of meat-offering of the pan belonging to the high priest.
verses.32: And Banaias the Caathite, from among their brethren, was set over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath.
verses.33: And these were the singers, heads of families of the Levites, to whom were established daily courses, for they were employed in the services day and night.
verses.34: These were the heads of the families of the Levites according to their generations; these chiefs dwelt in Jerusalem.
verses.35: And Jeël the father of Gabaon dwelt in Gabaon; and his wife's name was Moöcha.
verses.36: And his first-born son was Abdon, and he had Sur, and Kis, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab,
verses.37: and Gedur and his brother, and Zacchur, and Makeloth.
verses.38: And Makeloth begot Samaa: and these dwelt in the midst of their brethren in Jerusalem, even in the midst of their brethren.
verses.39: And Ner begot Kis, and Kis begot Saul, and Saul begot Jonathan, and Melchisue, and Aminadab, and Asabal.
verses.40: And the son of Jonathan was Meribaal: and Meribaal begot Micha.
verses.41: And the sons of Micha were Phithon and Malach, and Tharach.
verses.42: And Achaz begot Jada: and Jada begot Galemeth, and Gazmoth, and Zambri; and Zambri begot Massa.
verses.43: And Massa begot Baana, and Rhaphaïa was his son, Elasa his son, Esel his son.
verses.44: And Esel had six sons, and these were their names; Esricam his first-born, and Ismael, and Saraia, and Abdia, and Anan, and Asa: these were the sons of Esel.

verses.1: And it was told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines war in Keila, and they rob, they trample on the threshing-floors.
verses.2: And David enquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And the Lord said, Go, and thou shalt smite these Philistines, and shalt save Keila.
verses.3: And the men of David said to him, Behold, we are afraid here in Judea; and how shall it be if we go to Keila? shall we go after the spoils of the Philistines?
verses.4: And David enquired yet again of the Lord; and the Lord answered him, and said to him, Arise and go down to Keila, for I will deliver the Philistines into thy hands.
verses.5: So David and his men with him went to Keila, and fought with the Philistines; and they fled from before him, and he carried off their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter, and David rescued the inhabitants of Keila.
verses.6: And it came to pass when Abiathar the son of Achimelech fled to David, that he went down with David to Keila, having an ephod in his hand.
verses.7: And it was told Saul that David was come to Keila: and Saul said, God has sold him into my hands, for he is shut up, having entered into a city that has gates and bars.
verses.8: And Saul charged all the people to go down to war to Keila, to besiege David and his men.
verses.9: And David knew that Saul spoke openly of mischief against him: and David said to Abiathar the priest, Bring the ephod of the Lord.
verses.10: And David said, Lord God of Israel, thy servant has indeed heard, that Saul seeks to come against Keila to destroy the city on my account.
verses.11: Will the place be shut up? and now will Saul come down, as thy servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, tell thy servant. And the Lord said, It will be shut up.
verses.13: And David arose, and the men with him, in number about four hundred, and they went forth from Keila, and went whithersoever they could go: and it was told Saul that David had escaped from Keila, and he forbore to come.
verses.14: And he dwelt in Maserem in the wilderness, in the narrow passes; and dwelt in the wilderness in mount Ziph, in the dry country. And Saul sought him continually, but the Lord delivered him not into his hands.
verses.15: And David perceived that Saul went forth to seek David; and David was in the dry mountain in the New Ziph.
verses.16: And Jonathan son of Saul rose, and went to David to Cæne, and strengthened his hands in the Lord.
verses.17: And he said to him, Fear not, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be second to thee; and Saul my father knows it.
verses.18: So they both made a covenant before the Lord; and David dwelt in Cæne, and Jonathan went to his home.
verses.19: And the Ziphites came up out of the dry country to Saul to the hill, saying, Behold, is not David hidden with us in Messara, in the narrows in Cæne in the hill of Echela, which is on the right of Jessæmon?
verses.20: And now according to all the king's desire to come down, let him come down to us; they have shut him up into the hands of the king.
verses.21: And Saul said to them, Blessed be ye of the Lord, for ye have been grieved on my account.
verses.22: Go, I pray you, and make preparations yet, and notice his place where his foot shall be, quickly, in that place which ye spoke of, lest by any means he should deal craftily.
verses.23: Take notice, then, and learn, and I will go with you; and it shall come to pass that if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Juda.
verses.24: And the Ziphites arose, and went before Saul: and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, westward, to the right of Jessæmon.
verses.25: And Saul and his men went to seek him: and they brought word to David, and he went down to the rock that was in the wilderness of Maon: and Saul heard, and followed after David to the wilderness of Maon.
verses.26: And Saul and his men go on one side of the mountain, and David and his men are on the other side of the mountain: and David was hiding himself to escape from Saul: and Saul and his men encamped against David and his men, in order to take them.
verses.27: And there came a messenger to Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come hither, for the Philistines have invaded the land.
verses.28: So Saul returned from following after David, and went to meet the Philistines: therefore that place was called The divided Rock.

verses.1: And the Lord said to me, Though Moses and Samuel stood before my face, my soul could not be toward them: dismiss this people, and let them go forth.
verses.2: And it shall be, if they say to thee, Whither shall we go forth? then thou shalt say to them, Thus saith the Lord; As many as are for death, to death; and as many as are for famine, to famine; and as many as are for the sword, to the sword; and as many as are for captivity, to captivity.
verses.3: And I will punish them with four kinds of death, saith the Lord, the sword to slay, and the dogs to tear, and the wild beasts of the earth, and the birds of the sky to devour and destroy.
verses.4: And I will deliver them up for distress to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasses son of Ezekias king of Juda, for all that he did in Jerusalem.
verses.5: Who will spare thee, O Jerusalem? and who will fear for thee? or who will turn back to ask for thy welfare?
verses.6: Thou hast turned away from me, saith the Lord, thou wilt go back: therefore I will stretch out my hand, and will destroy thee, and will no more spare them.
verses.7: And I will completely scatter them; in the gates of my people they are bereaved of children: they have destroyed my people because of their iniquities.
verses.8: Their widows have been multiplied more than the sand of the sea: I have brought young men against the mother, even distress at noon-day: I have suddenly cast upon her trembling and anxiety.
verses.9: She that bore seven is spent; her soul has fainted under trouble; her sun is gone down while it is yet noon; she is ashamed and disgraced: I will give the remnant of them to the sword before their enemies.
verses.10: Woe is me, my mother! thou hast born me as some man of strife, and at variance with the whole earth; I have not helped others, nor has any one helped me; my strength has failed among them that curse me.
verses.11: Be it so, Lord, in their prosperity; surely I stood before thee in the time of their calamities, and in the time of their affliction, for their good against the enemy.
verses.12: Will iron be known? whereas thy strength is a brazen covering.
verses.13: Yea, I will give thy treasures for a spoil as a recompence, because of all thy sins, and that in all thy borders.
verses.14: And I will enslave thee to thine enemies round about, in a land which thou hast not known; for a fire has been kindled out of my wrath; it shall burn upon you.
verses.15: O Lord, remember me, and visit me, and vindicate me before them that persecute me; do not bear long with them; know how I have met with reproach for thy sake, from those who set at nought thy words;
verses.16: consume them; and thy word shall be to me for the joy and gladness of my heart: for thy name has been called upon me, O Lord Almighty.
verses.17: I have not sat in the assembly of them as they mocked, but I feared because of thy power: I sat alone, for I was filled with bitterness.
verses.18: Why do they that grieve me prevail against me? my wound is severe; whence shall I be healed? it is indeed become to me as deceitful water, that has no faithfulness.
verses.19: Therefore thus saith the Lord, If thou wilt return, then will I restore thee, and thou shalt stand before my face: and if thou wilt bring forth the precious from the worthless, thou shalt be as my mouth: and they shall return to thee; but thou shalt not return to them.
verses.20: And I will make thee to this people as a strong brazen wall; and they shall fight against thee, but they shall by no means prevail against thee;
verses.21: for I am with thee to save thee, and to deliver thee out of the hand of wicked men; and I will ransom thee out of the hand of pestilent men.

verses.1: The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Sedrach, and his sacrifice shall be in Damascus; for the Lord looks upon men, and upon all the tribes of Israel.
verses.2: And in Emath, even in her coasts, are Tyre and Sidon, because they were very wise.
verses.3: And Tyrus built strong-holds for herself, and heaped up silver as dust, and gathered gold as the mire of the ways.
verses.4: And therefore the Lord will take them for a possession, and will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be consumed with fire.
verses.5: Ascalon shall see, and fear; Gaza also, and shall be greatly pained, and Accaron; for she is ashamed at her trespass; and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ascalon shall not be inhabited.
verses.6: And aliens shall dwell in Azotus, and I will bring down the pride of the Philistines.
verses.7: And I will take their blood out of their mouth, and their abominations from between their teeth; and these also shall be left to our God, and they shall be as a captain of a thousand in Juda, and Accaron as a Jebusite.
verses.8: And I will set up a defence for my house, that they may not pass through, nor turn back, neither shall there any more come upon them one to drive them away: for now have I seen with mine eyes.
verses.9: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion; proclaim it aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem; behold, the King is coming to thee, just, and a Saviour; he is meek and riding on an ass, and a young foal.
verses.10: And he shall destroy the chariots out of Ephraim, and the horse out of Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be utterly destroyed; and there shall be abundance and peace out of the nations; and he shall rule over the waters as far as the sea, and the rivers to the ends of the earth.
verses.11: And thou by the blood of thy covenant hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit that has no water.
verses.12: Ye shall dwell in strongholds, ye prisoners of the congregation: and for one day of thy captivity I will recompense thee double.
verses.13: For I have bent thee, O Juda, for myself as a bow, I have filled Ephraim; and I will raise up thy children, O Sion, against the children of the Greeks, and I will handle thee as the sword of a warrior.
verses.14: And the Lord shall be over them, and his arrow shall go forth as lightning: and the Lord Almighty shall blow with the trumpet; and shall proceed with the tumult of his threatening.
verses.15: The Lord Almighty shall protect them, and they shall destroy them, and overwhelm them with sling-stones; and they shall swallow them down as wine, and fill the bowls as the altar.
verses.16: And the Lord their God shall save them in that day, even his people as a flock; for holy stones are rolled upon his land.
verses.17: For if he has anything good, and if he has anything fair, the young men shall have corn, and there shall be fragrant wine to the virgins.

verses.1: And it came to pass as David dwelt in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, Behold, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the Lord is under curtains of skins.
verses.2: And Nathan said to David, Do all that is in thy heart; for God is with thee.
verses.3: And it came to pass in that night, that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.4: Go and say to David my servant, Thus said the Lord, Thou shalt not build me a house for me to dwell in it.
verses.5: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up Israel until this day, but I have been in a tabernacle and a tent,
verses.6: in all places through which I have gone with all Israel: did I ever speak to any one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why is it that ye have not built me a house of cedar?
verses.7: And now thus shalt thou say to my servant David, Thus saith the Lord Almighty, I took thee from the sheepfold, from following the flocks, to be a ruler over my people Israel:
verses.8: and I was with thee in all places whither thou wentest, and I destroyed all thine enemies from before thee, and I made for thee a name according to the name of the great ones that are upon the earth.
verses.9: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant him, and he shall dwell by himself, and shall no longer be anxious; and the son of iniquity shall no longer afflict him, as at the beginning,
verses.10: and from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. Also I have humbled all thine enemies, and I will increase thee, and the Lord will build thee a house.
verses.11: And it shall come to pass when thy days shall be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, that I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall be of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.12: He shall build me a house, and I will set up his throne for ever.
verses.13: I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son: and my mercy will I not withdraw from him, as I withdrew it from them that were before thee.
verses.14: And I will establish him in my house and in his kingdom for ever; and his throne shall be set up for ever.
verses.15: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so spoke Nathan to David.
verses.16: And king David came and sat before the Lord, and said, Who am I, O Lord God? and what is my house, that thou hast loved me for ever?
verses.17: And these things were little in thy sight, O God: thou hast also spoken concerning the house of thy servant for a long time to come, and thou hast looked upon me as a man looks upon his fellow, and hast exalted me, O Lord God.
verses.18: What shall David do more toward thee to glorify thee? and thou knowest thy servant.
verses.19: And thou hast wrought all this greatness according to thine heart.
verses.20: O Lord, there is none like thee, and there is no God beside thee, according to all things which we have heard with our ears.
verses.21: Neither is there another nation upon the earth such as thy people Israel, whereas God led him in the way, to redeem a people for himself, to make for himself a great and glorious name, to cast out nations from before thy people, whom thou redeemedst out of Egypt.
verses.22: And thou hast appointed thy people Israel as a people to thyself for ever; and thou, Lord, didst become a God to them.
verses.23: And now, Lord, let the word which thou spokest to thy servant, and concerning his house, be confirmed for ever, and do thou as thou hast spoken.
verses.24: And let thy name be established and magnified for ever, men saying, Lord, Lord, Almighty God of Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.
verses.25: For thou, O Lord my God, hast revealed to the ear of thy servant that thou wilt build him a house; therefore thy servant has found a willingness to pray before thee.
verses.26: And now, Lord, thou thyself art God, and thou hast spoken these good things concerning thy servant.
verses.27: And now thou hast begun to bless the house of thy servant, so that it should continue for ever before thee: for thou, Lord, hast blessed it, and do thou bless it for ever.

verses.1: And it came to pass when the king sat in his house, and the Lord had given him an inheritance on every side free from all his enemies round about him;
verses.2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold now, I live in a house of cedar, and the ark of the Lord dwells in the midst of a tent.
verses.3: And Nathan said to the king, Go and do all that is in thine heart, for the Lord is with thee.
verses.4: And it came to pass in that night, that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.5: Go, and say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord, Thou shalt not build me a house for me to dwell in.
verses.6: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt to this day, but I have been walking in a lodge and in a tent,
verses.7: wheresoever I went with all Israel. Have I ever spoken to any of the tribes of Israel, which I commanded to tend my people Israel, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?
verses.8: And now thus shalt thou say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord Almighty, I took thee from the sheep-cote, that thou shouldest be a prince over my people, over Israel.
verses.9: And I was with thee wheresoever thou wentest, and I destroyed all thine enemies before thee, and I made thee renowned according to the renown of the great ones on the earth.
verses.10: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves, and shall be no more distressed; and the son of iniquity shall no more afflict them, as he has done from the beginning,
verses.11: from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel: and I will give thee rest from all thine enemies, and the Lord will tell thee that thou shalt build a house to him.
verses.12: And it shall come to pass when thy days shall have been fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, that I will raise up thy seed after thee, even thine own issue, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.13: He shall build for me a house to my name, and I will set up his throne even for ever.
verses.14: I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. And when he happens to transgress, then will I chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the sons of men.
verses.15: But my mercy I will not take from him, as I took it from those whom I removed from my presence.
verses.16: And his house shall be made sure, and his kingdom for ever before me, and his throne shall be set up for ever.
verses.17: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.18: And king David came in, and sat before the Lord, and said, Who am I, O Lord, my Lord, and what is my house, that thou hast loved me hitherto?
verses.19: Whereas I was very little before thee, O Lord, my Lord, yet thou spokest concerning the house of thy servant for a long time to come. And is this the law of man, O Lord, my Lord?
verses.20: And what shall David yet say to thee? and now thou knowest thy servant, O Lord, my Lord.
verses.21: And thou hast wrought for thy servant's sake, and according to thy heart thou hast wrought all this greatness, to make it known to thy servant,
verses.22: that he may magnify thee, O my Lord; for there is no one like thee, and there is no God but thou among all of whom we have heard with our ears.
verses.23: And what other nation in the earth is as thy people Israel? whereas God was his guide, to redeem for himself a people to make thee a name, to do mightily and nobly, so that thou shouldest cast out nations and their tabernacles from the presence of thy people, whom thou didst redeem for thyself out of Egypt?
verses.24: And thou hast prepared for thyself thy people Israel to be a people for ever, and thou, Lord, art become their God.
verses.25: And now, O my Lord, the Almighty Lord God of Israel, confirm the word for ever which thou hast spoken concerning thy servant and his house: and now as thou hast said,
verses.26: Let thy name be magnified for ever.
verses.27: Almighty Lord God of Israel, thou hast uncovered the ear of thy servant, saying, I will build thee a house: therefore thy servant has found in his heart to pray this prayer to thee.
verses.28: And now, O Lord my Lord, thou art God; and thy words will be true, and thou hast spoken these good things concerning thy servant.
verses.29: And now begin and bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee; for thou, O Lord, my Lord, hast spoken, and the house of thy servant shall be blessed with thy blessing so as to continue for ever.

verses.1: And Solomon the son of David was established over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him, and increased him exceedingly.
verses.2: And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the captains of thousands, and to the captains of hundreds, and to the judges, and to all the rulers over Israel, even the heads of the families;
verses.3: and Solomon and all the congregation went to the high place that was in Gabaon, where was God's tabernacle of witness, which Moses the servant of the Lord made in the wilderness.
verses.4: But David had brought up the ark of God out of the city of Cariathiarim; for David had prepared a place for it, for he had pitched a tabernacle for it in Jerusalem.
verses.5: And the brazen altar which Beseleel the son of Urias, the son of Or, had made, was there before the tabernacle of the Lord: and Solomon and the congregation enquired at it.
verses.6: And Solomon brought victims thither to the brazen altar that was before the Lord in the tabernacle, and offered upon it a thousand whole-burnt-offerings.
verses.7: In that night God appeared to Solomon, and said to him, Ask what I shall give thee.
verses.8: And Solomon said to God, Thou hast dealt very mercifully with my father David, and hast made me king in his stead.
verses.9: And now, O Lord God, let, I pray thee, thy name be established upon David my father; for thou hast made me king over a people numerous as the dust of the earth.
verses.10: Now give me wisdom and understanding, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who shall judge this thy great people?
verses.11: And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thy heart, and thou hast not asked great wealth, nor glory, nor the life of thine enemies, and thou hast not asked long life; but hast asked for thyself wisdom and understanding, that thou mightest judge my people, over whom I have made thee king:
verses.12: I give thee this wisdom and understanding; and I will give thee wealth, and riches, and glory, so that there shall not have been any like thee among the kings before thee, neither shall there be such after thee.
verses.13: And Solomon came from the high place that was in Gabaon to Jerusalem, from before the tabernacle of witness, and reigned over Israel.
verses.14: And Solomon collected chariots and horsemen: and he had fourteen hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen: and he set them in the cities of chariots, and the people were with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.15: And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem to be as stones, and cedars in Judea as sycamores in the plain for multitude.
verses.16: And Solomon imported horses from Egypt, and the charge of the king's merchants for going was as follows, and they traded,
verses.17: and went and brought out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty pieces of silver: and so they brought for all the kings of the Chettites, and for the kings of Syria by their means.
verses.18: And Solomon said that he would build a house to the name of the Lord, and a house for his kingdom.

verses.1: And he said to me, Son of man, eat this volume, and go and speak to the children of Israel.
verses.2: So he opened my mouth, and caused me to eat the volume. And he said to me, Son of man,
verses.3: thy mouth shall eat, and thy belly shall be filled with this volume that is given to thee. So I ate it; and it was in my mouth as sweet honey.
verses.4: And he said to me, Son of man, go thy way, and go in to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them.
verses.5: For thou art not sent to a people of hard speech, but to the house of Israel;
verses.6: neither to many nations of other speech and other tongues, nor of harsh language, whose words thou wouldest not understand: although if I had sent thee to such, they would have hearkened to thee.
verses.7: But the house of Israel will not be willing to hearken to thee; for they will not hearken to me: for all the house of Israel are stubborn and hard-hearted.
verses.8: And, behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen thy power against their power.
verses.9: And it shall be continually stronger than a rock: be not afraid of them, neither be dismayed at their faces, because it is a provoking house.
verses.10: And he said to me, Son of man, receive into thine heart all the words that I have spoken to thee, and hear them with thine ears.
verses.11: And go thy way, go in to the captivity, to the children of thy people, and thou shalt speak to them, and say to them, Thus saith the Lord; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.
verses.12: Then the Spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the voice as of a great earthquake, saying, Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place.
verses.13: And I perceived the sound of the wings of the living creatures clapping one to the other, and the sound of the wheels was near them, and the sound of the earthquake.
verses.14: And the Spirit lifted me, and took me up, and I went in the impulse of my spirit; and the hand of the Lord was mighty upon me.
verses.15: Then I passed through the air and came into the captivity, and went round to them that dwelt by the river of Chobar who were there; and I sat there seven days, conversant in the midst of them.
verses.16: And after the seven days the word of the Lord came to me, saying, Son of man,
verses.17: I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel; and thou shalt hear a word of my mouth, and shalt threaten them from me.
verses.18: When I say to the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou hast not warned him, to give warning to the wicked, to turn from his ways, that he should live; that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thy hand.
verses.19: But if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, and from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, and thou shalt deliver thy soul.
verses.20: And when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits a trespass, and I shall bring punishment before him, he shall die, because thou didst not warn him: he shall even die in his sins, because his righteousness shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thine hand.
verses.21: But if thou warn the righteous not to sin, and he sin not, the righteous shall surely live, because thou hast warned him; and thou shalt deliver thine own soul.
verses.22: And the hand of the Lord came upon me; and he said to me, Arise, and go forth into the plain, and there shalt thou be spoken to.
verses.23: And I arose, and went forth to the plain: and, behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, according to the vision, and according to the glory of the Lord, which I saw by the river of Chobar: and I fell on my face.
verses.24: Then the Spirit came upon me, and set me on my feet, and spoke to me, and said to me, Go in, and shut thyself up in the midst of thine house.
verses.25: And thou, son of man, behold, bonds are prepared for thee, and they shall bind thee with them, and thou shalt not come forth of the midst of them.
verses.26: Also I will bind thy tongue, and thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them a reprover: because it is a provoking house.
verses.27: But when I speak to thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say to them, Thus saith the Lord, He that hears, let him hear; and he that is disobedient, let him be disobedient: because it is a provoking house.

verses.1: Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying, Also, thou, son of man, say,
verses.2: Thus saith the Lord; An end is come to the land of Israel, the end is come on the four corners of the land.
verses.3: The end is come
verses.4: on thee, the inhabitant of the land: the time is come, the day has drawn nigh, not with tumult, nor with pangs.
verses.5: Now I will pour out mine anger upon thee near at hand, and I will accomplish my wrath on thee: and I will judge thee for thy ways, and recompense upon thee all thine abominations.
verses.6: Mine eye shall not spare, nor will I have any mercy: for I will recompense thy ways upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord that smite thee.
verses.7: Now the end is come to thee, and I will send judgment upon thee: and I will take vengeance on thy ways, and will recompense all thine abominations upon thee.
verses.8: Mine eye shall not spare, nor will I have any mercy: for I will recompense thy way upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
verses.9: For thus saith the Lord; Behold, the end is come.
verses.10: Behold, the day of the Lord! although the rod has blossomed,
verses.11: pride has sprung up, and will break the staff of the wicked one, and that not with tumult, nor with haste.
verses.12: The time is come, behold the day: let not the buyer rejoice, and let not the seller mourn.
verses.13: For the buyer shall never again return to the seller, neither shall a man cleave with the eye of hope to his life.
verses.14: Sound ye the trumpet, and pass sentence on all together.
verses.15: There shall be war with the sword without, and famine and pestilence within: he that is in the field shall die by the sword; and famine and pestilence shall destroy them that are in the city.
verses.16: But they that escape of them shall be delivered, and shall be upon the mountains: and I will slay all the rest, every one for his iniquities.
verses.17: All hands shall be completely weakened, and all thighs shall be defiled with moisture.
verses.18: And they shall gird themselves with sackcloth, and amazement shall cover them; and shame shall be upon them, even upon every face, and baldness upon every head.
verses.19: Their silver shall be cast forth in the streets, and their gold shall be despised: their souls shall not be satisfied, and their bellies shall not be filled: for it was the punishment of their iniquities.
verses.20: As for their choice ornaments, they employed them for pride, and they made of them images of their abominations: therefore have I made them uncleanness to them.
verses.21: And I will deliver them into the hands of strangers to make them a prey, and to the pests of the earth for a spoil; and they shall profane them.
verses.22: And I will turn away my face from them, and they shall defile my charge, and shall go in to them unguardedly, and profane them.
verses.23: And they shall work uncleanness: because the land is full of strange nations, and the city is full of iniquity.
verses.24: And I will turn back the boasting of their strength; and their holy things shall be defiled.
verses.25: And though propitiation shall come, and one shall seek peace, yet there shall be none.
verses.26: There shall be woe upon woe, and there shall be message upon message; and a vision shall be sought from a prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.
verses.27: The prince shall clothe himself with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be made feeble: I will do to them according to their ways, and according to their judgments will I punish them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

verses.1: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.2: Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it,
verses.3: and say to it, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, O mount Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against thee, and will make thee a waste, and thou shalt be made desolate.
verses.4: And I will cause desolation in thy cities, and thou shalt be desolate, and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
verses.5: Because thou hast been a perpetual enemy, and hast laid wait craftily for the house of Israel, with the hand of enemies with a sword, in the time of injustice, at the last:
verses.6: Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, verily thou hast sinned even to blood, therefore blood shall pursue thee.
verses.7: And I will make mount Seir a waste, and desolate, and I will destroy from off it men and cattle:
verses.8: and I will fill thy hills and thy valleys with slain men, and in all thy plains there shall fall in thee men slain with the sword.
verses.9: I will make thee a perpetual desolation, and thy cities shall not be inhabited any more: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
verses.10: Because thou saidst, The two nations and the two countries shall be mine, and I shall inherit them; whereas the Lord is there:
verses.11: therefore, as I live, saith the Lord, I will even deal with thee according to thine enmity, and I will be made known to thee when I shall judge thee:
verses.12: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord. I have heard the voice of thy blasphemies, whereas thou hast said, The desert mountains of Israel are given to us for food;
verses.13: and thou hast spoken swelling words against me with thy mouth: I have heard them.
verses.14: Thus saith the Lord; When all the earth is rejoicing, I will make thee desert.
verses.15: Thou shalt be desert, O mount Seir, and all Idumea; and it shall be utterly consumed: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord their God.
